courses.label: ME 566
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics 3
paras: Reynolds stresses, intensity and scale of turbulence. The “law of the wail”, logarithmic velocity profile and velocrity defect laws, effects of roughness. Pressure loss in pipes and conduits. Jets and wakes. Flow in diffusers and contractions, and experimental measurement techniques.

courses.label: ME 568
courses.title: Noise Analysis and Control
paras: Basic acoustics. Legal aspects. Physiology of the ear. Signal analysis. Instruments and techniques. Noise reduction techniques, absorption, damping and barrier. Wave transmission and impedance. Handling industrial plant noise problems. Designing for minimum noise in engineering systems.

courses.label: ME 569
courses.title: Fluid Mechanics-Design Topics
paras: A study of the design aspects of fluid mechanics, Unsteady flow, pipe and duct systems, two and three dimensional flow techniques, practical calculation of boundary layers, separa~ tion, base pressures, jets, wakes and shear layers, diffusers and flow distribution devices, flow control, twophase flow, instrumentation, wind tunnel modelling, wind loading. The course will be oriented to practical design techniques for flow systems, reactors, air pollution control equipment, etc.

courses.label: ME 571
courses.title: Air Pollution 1
paras: Nature and sources of air pollution, chemical and biological aspects, effects on heaith and environment. Physical aspects of the atmosphere, thermodynamics, vertical variation of wind and temperature, stability, convection, atmospheric turbulence, diffusion equations, plumes, thermals, jets in stratified flow, radioactive plumes, particulate dispersion, instrumentation (micrometeorological), air pollution control techniques and equipment monitoring instrumentation.

courses.label: OPTOM 100
courses.title: History and Orientation
paras: A brief history of the profession and the development of visual science; a consideration of legal and organizational development of optometry; the role of professional associations. The role and scope of optometry and its relationship to other professions and the community.

courses.label: OPTOM 104
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: The gross, microscopic and ultra structure of ocular tissues. The embryology and comparative anatomy of the eye will be emphasized. The relationship of the eye to the vascular supply of the head and the nervous system witl be studied. This course is credited only upon completion of OPTOM 114.
Prereq: BIOL 201

courses.label: OPTOM 105
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: Basic disease processes, including inflammation, degeneration, neoplasia; pathogenic microbiology and related diseases; immunity and hypersensitivity; disease caused by physical agents; diseases of the organ systems.
Prereq: BIOL 201.

courses.label: OPTOM 106
courses.title: Geometrical Optics
paras: Reflection and refraction. Image formation. Optical properties of plane and curved surfaces, prisms and thin lenses. Thick lens theory and lens systems. Ray construction. Optical and ophthalmic instruments. Polarization. Prereqg: PHYS 121, 121L, 122, 122L, MATH 113.

courses.label: OPTOM 111
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The eye as an optical instrument. Ametropia and emmetropia. The refracting mechanism. The stimulus to accommodation. Ocular transmission. Visual acuity and visual performance; stray light in the eye; analysis of the retinal stimulus pattern.
Prereq: OPTOM 106

courses.label: OPTOM 114
courses.title: Anatomy of the Eye and Associated Structures
paras: A continuation of Optom 104. Prereq: OPTOM 104

courses.label: OPTOM 115
courses.title: General Pathology
paras: A continuation of 105. Prereq: OPTOM 105.

courses.label: OPTOM 116
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: Properties of optical glass and plastic, single vision lenses and prisms, lens combinations. Optics of contact lenses and clinical instruments. Ophthalmic laboratory procedures.

courses.label: OPTOM 241
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: Ocular motility: Kinematics of eye movements, muscle actions, measurements of eye movements, types of eye movements, innervational systems subserving eye movements, clinical application. ‘
Prereq: OPTOM 111

courses.label: OPTOM 242
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Lectures and laboratories on clinical techniques for examination of the optical properties of the eye. Prereq: OPTOM 111

courses.label: OPTOM 244
courses.title: Neurophysiology of Vision
paras: The neural processing of colour, brightness, movement and form by the retina, lateral geniculate, cortex, superior colliculus and other brain centres. Neural Mechanisms underlying binocular depth perception, the accommodative response and eye movement.
Prereq: OPTOM 104/114

courses.label: OPTOM 245
courses.title: - Ocular Pathology
paras: Signs, symptoms, Clinical detection of primary and secondary ocular disease; instrument techniques; record keeping, patient Counselling, referral procedures; management of ocular emergencies; primary health care responsibilities. Prereq: OPTOM 105/115

courses.label: OPTOM 246
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: Optica! problems in bifocals, multifocals and progressive addition lenses. Lenses for aphakics. Absorptive lenses. Aberrations of thin lenses and best performance design. Optics of low vision devices.
Prereq: OPTOM 116
Course Descriptions
Optometry

courses.label: OPTOM 251
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The retinal stimulus pattern. Visual perception. Mach theory. Binocular vision. stereopsis, binocular integration. binocular space perception. Theory of aniseikonia. Perceptual aspects of aniseikonia. Visual illusions.

courses.label: OPTOM 252
courses.title: Clinical Optometry
paras: Clinical techniques for the examination of the binocular relations of the nonstrabismic patient, with particular emphasis on the study of the relationship between accommodation and convergence. Techniques of phorometry, prism vergence texts, relative accommodation tests, retinoscopy, and monocular and binocular cross cylinder tests.
Prereq: OPTOM 241/242

courses.label: OPTOM 254
courses.title: Physiology of The Eye and Ocular Adnexa
paras: The physiology of the smooth muscles of the eye, the extraocular striate muscles, the lacrimai apparatus, the cornea, the iris, the lens, the ciliary body and the vitreous body. Production and drainage of aqueous and related influences on intraocular pressure. The vascular supply of the eye.
Prereq: OPTOM 104

courses.label: OPTOM 255
courses.title: Ocular Pathology
paras: A continuation of 245. Prereq: OPTOM 245

courses.label: OPTOM 259
paras: Light and lilumination
Principles of radiometry and photometry; illumination and related factors involved in the design and control of the visual environment in relationship to the human visual system; lighting surveys.

courses.label: OPTOM 261
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: The perception of light. Spectral sensitivity of the eye. Photochemistry of the retina. Luminance discrimination. The Stiles-Crawford effect. Visual Acuity. Intermittent stimulation. Introduction to colorimetry.

courses.label: OPTOM 274
courses.title: Genetics for Optometrists
paras: A brief review of Mendelian genetics, and the molecular basis of modern genetics. Inherited conditions of
particular interest, e.g., colour vision, albinism, aniridia, refractive error, retinoblastoma. Genetic counselling, and the detection of carriers.
Prereq: OPTOM 245

courses.label: OPTOM 342
courses.title: Clinical Optometry: Case Analysis
paras: Presentations with problem solving sessions Concerning the analysis of examination data gathered for a nonstrabismic patient. Issues relevant to diagnoses, modes of therapy, prognosis and counselling will be emphasized.

courses.label: OPTOM 344
courses.title: Sensory Physiology
paras: Peripheral and central nervous system pathways. The skin senses, pain and adaptation to pain, especiaily as they relate to cornea. The vestibular sense and its influence on eye-movements, muscle sensory organs, including those in extra-ocular muscles, audition, olfaction, taste, visceral sensations and the origin of headaches.

courses.label: OPTOM 346
courses.title: Optometrical Optics
paras: The lecture course deais with problems involved in selecting, preparing and fitting ophthalmic materials. Optical, cosmetic and comfort requirements, and patient counselling are considered. Labs provide experience in preparing and fitting materials to patients.
Prereq: OPTOM 116, 246

courses.label: OPTOM 347
courses.title: Optometric Specialties: Contact Lenses
paras: A series of lectures and laboratories on the principles and procedures of prescribing and fitting contact lenses.

courses.label: OPTOM 348
courses.title: Optometric Clinic and Optometric Communication
paras: The student is assigned to the various areas of the clinic and under the direct supervision of optometrists of the clinic staff, carries out routine clinical investigations of patients. Lectures will follow the outline of Optometry 513. Prereq: OPTOM 242, 252

courses.label: OPTOM 350
courses.title: Optometrical Jurisprudence and Praxis
paras: Legal aspects of practising optometry in Canada. Practice management. Financial management. Interprofessional relations. Office design. Optometric assistants. Professional associations.

courses.label: OPTOM 351W
courses.title: Physiological Optics
paras: Increment thresholds and Stiles mechanisms. Laws of colour mixture. Chromaticity diagrams. Colour matching and colour discrimination. Characteristics of normals and colour defectives. The design of visual colorimeters, anomaloscopes and of colour vision screening tests. Congenital and acquired defects of colour vision. Prereg: OPTOM 267

courses.label: OPTOM 352
courses.title: Clinical Optom: Strabismus and Orthoptics
paras: Detection and evaluation of sensory and motor characteristics of vision in strabismus. Classifications, diagnosis, prognosis, modes of therapy for strabismus and amblyopia.
Prereq: OPTOM 242, 252, 342.

courses.label: OPTOM 357
courses.title: Optometric Specialties: Aniseikonia and Low Vision Aids
paras: A series of tectures and labs in examining low vision and aniseikonic patients with specific techniques described. Treatment and therapy will be included. Prereq: OPTOM 342

courses.label: OPTOM 358
paras: Each student is required to complete 120 hours of clinical practice during the spring.
Prereq: Successful completion of
Year 3.

courses.label: OPTOM 364
courses.title: Ocular Pharmacology
paras: Neurohumoral theory, response to drugs, use of sterile techniques, disinfectants. Drugs used topically on the eye. Systemically administered drugs which may affect the eye and vision. Drugs and contact lenses.
Prereq: OPTOM 245, 255

courses.label: OPTOM 372
courses.title: Pediatric Optometry
paras: Special aspects of the management of vision problems of infants and young children.
Prereq: OPTOM 242, 252

courses.label: OPTOM 500
courses.title: Optometrical Praxis
paras: Practice management; financial management, establishing a practice, interprofessional relations, office design, optometric assistants, professional associations.

courses.label: OPTOM 501
courses.title: Optometry Research Project
paras: Students with an interest in research may arrange with a professor to undertake a research project of mutual interest. This course serves as an alternative to PSYCH 357. Contact the course co-ordinator for details.

courses.label: OPTOM 502
courses.title: Advanced Contact Lens Practice
paras: A series of lectures and practica! demonstrations of the principles and procedures of advanced contact lens materials and resources including their physiological implications.
Pediatric Optometry
Special aspects of the management of vision problems of infants and young children are discussed.

Visual Aspects of Learning Difficulties The aspects of vision problems related to learning difficulty including tests and measurements taken by optometrists. The role of the optometrist in conjunction with the parents, teachers, and psychologits in assisting children to achieve is discussed.
Prereq: OPTOM 242, 252, 342, 352

courses.label: OPTOM 504
courses.title: Ocular Pharmacology
paras: Neurohumoral theory, response to drugs, use of sterile techniques, disinfectants. Drugs used topically on the eye. Systemically administered drugs which may affect the eye and vision. Drugs and contact lenses. Prereq: OPTOM 245, 255

courses.label: OPTOM 508
courses.title: Optometry Clinic
paras: The clinical program teaches the student how to provide optometrical services including pathology detection, strabismus evaluation and the application of spectacle therapy, contact lenses and vision training. The patients cared for extend from the pediatric to the geriatric, and include those with perceptual problems, or with tow vision. No credit given until successful completion of OPTOM 518. Prereq: OPTOM 348, 358

courses.label: OPTOM 509
courses.title: Community Health Optometry
paras: Governmental and social aspects of health and vision care delivery are discussed in relation to the epidemiology of vision problems.

courses.label: OPTOM 510
courses.title: Optometrical Jurisprudence
paras: Lectures relating to the legal aspects of practising optometry in Canada. The rights and responsibilities of the optometrist in practice are examined and discussed.

courses.label: OPTOM 511
courses.title: Optometry Research Project
paras: A continuation of 501. This course serves as an alternative to OPTOM 513. Prereq: OPTOM 501

courses.label: OPTOM 512
courses.title: Advanced Contact Lens Practice
paras: A continuation of OPTOM 502 with an emphasis on research.
Visual Gerontology
Aspects of the aging process on the visual system and the optometrical management of the visual problems of older persons.

courses.label: OPTOM 513
courses.title: Optometric Communication
paras: A series of presentations on verbal and nonverbal communication during the optometric examination and counselling of patients. Video-taped clinical performance will provide opportunity for peer and self-evaluation of communication skills. Patient management problems such as compliance and interprofessional communications.

courses.label: OPTOM 514
courses.title: Genetics for Optometrists
paras: A brief review of Mendelian genetics, and the molecular basis of modern genetics. Inherited conditions of particular interest, e.g., colour vision, albinism, aniridia, refractive error, retinoblastoma. Genetic counselling, and the detection of carriers.
Prereq: OPTOM 245

courses.label: OPTOM 518
courses.title: Optometry Clinic
paras: A continuation of 508.
Prereq: OPTOM 508

courses.label: OPTOM 519
paras: Aspects of prevention of accidents and injury to the visual system.
The production of efficient and comforatable vision at work and recreation.

courses.label: OPTOM 538
courses.title: Vision Care Projects
paras: All students are required to participate in vision care projects between the fourth and fifth professional years. These will invoive a minimum of 400 hours and will be arranged by the faculty.
Prereg. Successful completion of Optometry 348 and 358 and permission of the Chief of Clinics.

These examinations are ordinarily held in the final examination period of the Winter term, fourth professional year. These examinations have been approved for purposes of licensure for 1982 by the Council of the College of Optometrists of Ontario. .

Core Courses

The Core Courses for each year of the program are designed to bring together students from various disciplines who are interested in the problems of conflict and peace, with the objective of acquainting them with other disciplinary approaches to those problems. Core courses are taught in Conrad Grebel Callege by members of the PACS Faculty Group, other qualified and interested members of participating departments, or by eminent scholars in the field who will be invited to the University from time to time.

courses.label: PACS 201
courses.title: Roots of Conflict and Violence
paras: An examination of influentiai theories of the nature and roots of human conflict on both the interpersonal and intergroup level. Contributions of the behavioural and social sciences, as welt as the humanities, will be explored.

courses.label: PACS 202
courses.title: Conflict Resolution
paras: A continuation of PACS 201, with special emphasis on the means of conflict resolution or management. Included are critical assessments of negotiation, arbitration, confrontation, litigation, violence and nonviolent resistance, and other models of conflict resolution.

courses.label: PACS 301
courses.title: Special Topics in Peace and Conflict Studies 1
paras: A seminar course investigating special issues related to peace and conflict. The content of this and PACS 302 wilt vary from year to year as specialists in various aspects of these issues are invited to teach the courses.

courses.label: PACS 302
courses.title: Special Topics in Peace and Conflict Studies 2
paras: (Same as 301, above)

courses.label: PACS 498
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar 1
paras: Each Honours student will work on a research paper and will meet regularly with other students working on similar projects to discuss and evaluate his own work.

courses.label: PACS 499
courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar 2
paras: Continuation of PACS 498.
Peace and Conflict Studies Content Courses Offered by PACS
In addition to the Core Courses, the PACS Program offers the following Interdisciplinary PACS-related courses which may be used to fulfill the PACS Content Course requirements.

courses.label: PACS 230
courses.title: The Politics of Nonviolence
paras: An examination of the possibilities of a nonviolent approach to resolving human conflict with special emphasis on the nature and uses of power, the nature of the nation state, and the problem of relating a personal ideal to the realities of communal life.

courses.label: PACS 271
courses.title: Introduction to Peace Research 1
paras: A study of Current research in the developing field of “peace research" including studies of personality and agression, international tension, causes and, predictability of war, United Nations voting patterns, disarmament studies, and peace activism.

courses.label: PACS 272
courses.title: Introduction to Peace Research 2
paras: A continuation of PACS 271, above.

courses.label: PACS 398
courses.title: Directed Readings in Peace and Conflict Studies
paras: Students may arrange independent Studies in the area of peace and conflict studies on probiems of special interest. Students may also register under these numbers in order to repeat PACS 301 and/or 302.
Peace and Conflict Studies Content Courses Offered by Participating Departments

The following PACS-reiated courses are offered by the participating departments under their own designations. Additions or deletions may occur following the suggestion of the departments concerned and approval by the PACS Faculty Group. Full course descriptions are found in the departmental sections elsewhere in this chapter.

courses.label: PHIL 101X

courses.label: PHIL 102A
courses.title: Introduction: Knowledge and Reality
paras: Discussion of the nature of reality. Rival theories concerning mind, matter, freedom, the existence of God, and the place of experience and reason in human knowledge are considered

courses.label: PHIL 102B
courses.title: Introduction to Social and Political Philosophy
paras: An introduction to basic concepts and principles in classic and contemporary social and political philosophy. Differing views on basic questions are examined, with applications to such issues as capital punishment, welfare provisions, taxation, natural resource ownership, and terrorism.

courses.label: PHIL 102C
courses.title: Philosophy of Lite
paras: “Who am I?" “What can | hope for after death?" “How can | tell what to do?” “What can | know?” are questions that nave led many to philosophize. The course will examine what lifestyles and attitudes major philosophers, stoics, skeptics, pleasure-seekers, mystics, pragmatists, etc. have promoted, and why.
PHIL 1020 W 3C 05
Introduction to the Philosophy of Religion

Beginning with a consideration of such contemporary religious and antireligious options as secularism, mysticism, occultism, and charismatic renewal, this course moves to a critical discussion of such topics as religious experience, faith, God, and miracles.

courses.label: PHIL 140
courses.title: Introduction to Formal Logic
paras: Elementary sentence and predicate logic. Translation from English into the formalism, decision methods and deductions. Application of Graphic Methods to Logic. This course is a preparation for courses in the foundations of mathematics, scientific. methods, and more advanced logic courses.

courses.label: PHIL 145
courses.title: Critical Thinking
paras: An analysis af basic types of reasoning, structure of arguments, critical assessment of information, common fallacies, problems of clarity and meaning.

courses.label: PHIL 200
courses.title: Great Works of Western Philosophy
paras: An examination of some of the greatest writings in Western Philosophy. Students will be encouraged to come toa critical appreciation of such masterworks as Plato’s Republic, Descartes’ Discourse on Method, Hobbes’ Leviathan, Hume's Enquiry, Kant’s Prolegomena, Nietzsche's Zarathustra, and an outstanding work in contemporary philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 200A
paras: Great Works of Western Philosophy: Part 1
Outstanding works from the ancient and mediaeval periods.

courses.label: PHIL 200B
paras: Great Works of Western Philosophy: Part 11
Outstanding works from the early modern and contemporary periods.
Course Descriptions
Philosophy
Note Either PHIL 200A or PHiL 200B may be taken separately.
PHIL 201 Love

A philosophical analysis of different forms and functions of love. Among the topics to be considered; love and sexuality, religious love, love and knowledge. Ciassical and contemporary sources will be treated.

courses.label: PHIL 202
courses.title: Philosophy of Women
paras: A study of some of the issues raised by the Women's Liberation movement. Philosophical writings of the past and present will be used on such subjects as: the two sexes, physiological femininity, personal and social relations between the sexes, the position of women in public life, marriage and its alternatives, the importance of childbearing.

courses.label: PHIL 203
courses.title: Philosophical Perspectives on Death
paras: This course critically examines how philosophers from the Pre-Socratics to Wittgenstein have analysed the concept of death. The course is also concerned with topics like the concept of a person, personal identity, and survival after death.

courses.label: PHIL 205
courses.title: Science, Technology, and Society
paras: Alternative philosophical perspectives on problems raised by scientific and technological developments including moral issues (e.g. privacy and datagathering, ‘clean’ vs. ‘dirty’ energy.) Also an examination of the nature and scope of scientific and technical knowledge as it bears on the responsibilities of scientists and engineers.

courses.label: PHIL 210
courses.title: Philosophy in Literature
paras: Each term philosophical themes (such as alienation, freedom, and responsibility) will be explored through appropriate Jiterary works (e.g. works by Camus, Dostoevsky, Kafka, and Sartre).

courses.label: PHIL 215
courses.title: Professional and Business Ethics
paras: Study of ethical and moral issues that typically arise in professional and business activity. What responsibilities to society at large do people in such
business and professional activities as teaching, engineering, planning, architecture, and accounting have? How far should professional autonomy extend?

courses.label: PHIL 216
courses.title: Rational Behaviour and Decision-Making
paras: An elementary introduction to the subject of ‘rational’ behaviour and decision-making for individuals and groups. Emphasis is on the definition and measurement of utility functions and various criteria employed in models of decision-making. This course is intended to help those whose work will involve them in making decisions in either the public-or private sectors.

courses.label: PHIL 220
paras: Morat issues

The aim of this course is to improve the student's understanding of ethical ideas and principles by careful discussion of selected concrete moral issues, such as" abortion, euthanasia, capital punishment, and violence. Choice of issues is partly determined by student interest.

courses.label: PHIL 221
courses.title: Ethics 1
paras: This course is intended to be both a history of and an introduction to moral philosophy. Views on the foundations of ethics of the great philosophers fram classical antiquity to about 1900 are systematically examined. Writers studied include: Plato, Aristotle, Aquinas, Kant, Mill and-Nietzsche.

courses.label: PHIL 224
courses.title: Mankind and Nature
paras: An examination of some of the issues raised by recent discussions on ecology. Various theories of nature, the human being, and relations between the two will be explored. Possible foundations for duties of mankind toward nature will be examined.

courses.label: PHIL 225
paras: Social and Political Philosophy: Canadian Problems

Basic ideological perspectives - conservative, socialist, and liberal - on Canadian problems - such as native rights, nationalism, separatism, and regionalism - are philosophically presented and assessed.
Prereq: PHIL 102B or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 226
courses.title: Ethics and the Lite Sciences
paras: An investigation of some critical ethical issues in human research and therapy. Includes discussions of the right to live and right to die, behaviour control (e.g. psychosurgery, behaviour modification and psychotherapy), human experimentation (including “informed consent” and fetal research) and genetic engineering.
Prereq: One of PHIL 102B, 221, 322, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 236
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion: The Occult
paras: A critical philosophical discussion of reports of several kinds of extraordinary experiences, such as magic, extrasenory perception, mysticism, and divination will lead us to discussions of such concepts as insanity, irrationality, the supernatural, and the miraculous.

courses.label: PHIL 240
courses.title: Logic
paras: A systematic development of the propositional calculus and of the firstorder functional calculus. Some attention will be devoted to extensions and interpretations of such formal systems.
Prereq: None for second-year students and above; consent of instructor for others.

courses.label: PHIL 241
courses.title: Intermediate Logic
paras: Axiom systems of logic are developed and compared with natural deduction procedures. Then certain properties of these logical systems, such as consistency, completeness, and compactness, wil! be investigated. Prereq: PHIL 140 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 242
courses.title: Extensions and Applications of
paras: Elementary Logic : The classical logic introduced in PHIL 140 will be extended to form systems of modal logic, including logics of obligation, belief and knowledge, necessity, and temporal order. Essentialism, future contingencies, proofs for the existence of God will be discussed.
Prereq: PHIL 140 or consent of the instructor.
Course Descriptions
Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 243
courses.title: Conflict, Contract and Choice
paras: Basic concepts of game and decision theory are introduced and applied to ethical theory and problems in social philosophy.
Prereq: PHIL 140, 145 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 258
courses.title: Introduction to the Philosophy of Science
paras: A discussion of the fundamental concepts on which science is based. Consideration is given to such topics as scientific theories, the nature of lawlikeness, the grounds for scientific confirmation, and the debate between rationalism and empiricism in science.

courses.label: PHIL 265
courses.title: The Existentialist Experience
paras: An introduction to the existentialist view of man using both literary and philosophical texts from such authors as Kierkegaard, Unamuno, Nietzsche, Ortega y Gasset, Camus, Sartre, Heidegger and others.

courses.label: PHIL 300
courses.title: The Philosophy of Games
paras: An introduction to philosophical issues relating to sports and other games. Among the issues examined will be the nature of games, games and sports, and the relevance of games and sports to other philosophical! interests: e.g., ethics and aesthetics.

courses.label: PHIL 302
courses.title: Modern Feminism
paras: An examination of contemporary feminist thought, de Beauvoir through to the present. Positions taken on various issues will be compared and critically assessed.
Prereq: Second year standing or PHIL 202.

courses.label: PHIL 311
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 1
paras: A philosophical analysis of classical and contemporary theories of education, with a view to formulating a clear workable concept of education, its aims and methods.
Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 312
courses.title: Philosophy of Education 2
paras: An introduction to current work in the field, particularly that of Peters, Hirst.
and Dearden. Special attention will be
paid to the question of the desirability of a core curriculum and its proposed content.
Prereq: PHIL 311 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 322
courses.title: Contemporary Ethical Theory
paras: Continues the history and discussion of ethics begun in PHIL 221 with writings from 1900 to the present. Theories such as intuitionism, emotivism, utilitarianism, and relativism are examined via the writings of such people as Moore, Hare and Warnock.
Prereq: PHIL 221 recommended.

courses.label: PHIL 327A
courses.title: Philosophy of Law - Part 1
paras: An investigation of alternative views of law and legal reasoning forms the core of this course. Law's relations to morality, social practice, and politics are considered. Authors to be studied include Aquinas, Kart, Austin, and Hart.
Note This is a required course for the Legal Studies Option.

courses.label: PHIL 327B
courses.title: Philosophy of Law - Part 2
paras: An examination of areas within the law in which philosophical problems and methods are featured prominently. Topics such as liberty, responsibility and liability, punishment, rights and possession are considered.
Prereq: PHIL 327A or consent of the
instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 328
courses.title: The Philosophy of Karl Marx
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PHIL 329
courses.title: War, Peace and Justice
paras: An intensive study of the moral issues involved in war and armed revolution. Critical evaluation of “just war" theories, and international rules of warfare is pursued as well as the moral arguments for and against pacifism and conscientious objection.
Prereq: PHIL 102B, or 322 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 331
courses.title: Aesthetics
paras: Philosophical consideration of works of art and the problems of beauty using selected readings to enable the student to recognize and formulate his own views in a philosophic manner.
Prereq: One full or two half Philosophy courses, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 335
courses.title: Philosophy of Religion
paras: A critical examination of the methods and substantive arguments found in selected major works of religious philosophy. The writings chosen for consideration will be announced in advance each year.
Prereq: One full or two half Philosophy courses, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 350
courses.title: Epistemology
paras: An analysis of human knowledge, its conditions and types. The first part concentrates on criteria of meaningfulness, the possibility of a priori knowledge, and the concept of knowledge. The second part deals with our knowledge of the physical world and other minds.
Prereq: One full or two half courses in Philosophy.

courses.label: PHIL 350A
courses.title: Epistemology 1
paras: The first part of PHIL 350.

courses.label: PHIL 350B
courses.title: Epistemology 2
paras: The second part of PHIL 350.
Note Either 350A or 350B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 359
courses.title: Philosophy of the Formal Sciences
paras: A study of philosophical problems concerning mathematics. Topics discussed include formalism, intuitionism, logicism, the mathematical paradoxes, and other topics in foundations and metamathematics. Prereq: At least second year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 362
courses.title: Philosophy of the Social Sciences
paras: Problems about the fundamental methods and aims of the social sciences generally, and problems specific to Psychology, Sociology, Political Science, etc., and their relations to one another will be considered. (Cross-listed as SOC 371)

courses.label: PHIL 365
courses.title: Oriental Philosophy »

Chinese). Parailels will be drawn between modes of Eastern thinking and European conceptions with emphasis on essential differences as well as similarities.

courses.label: PHIL 381
courses.title: History of Ancient Philosophy 2
paras: Cross-listed as C CIV 362.

courses.label: PHIL 382
courses.title: Medieval Philosophy 1
paras: The early period of the 13th century. Among those considered will be: Augustine, Boethius, Anselm, and Abailard. Prereq: One half caurse in Philosophy, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 383
courses.title: Medieval Philosophy 2
paras: The later period from the 13th century. Among those considered will be: Bonaventure, Aquinas, Scotus, and Ockham.
Prereq: One half course in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 384
courses.title: History of Modern Philosophy 1
paras: Earlier period beginning with Descartes.
Prereq: One half course in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 385
courses.title: History of Modern Philosophy 2
paras: Later period including Hume and Kant. Prereq: One half course in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 386
courses.title: 19th Century Philosophy
paras: The 19th century. Philosophers covered may include Hegel, Mill, Schopenhauer, James, and Kierkegaard.
Prereq: One half course in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 420
courses.title: Studies in Ethics
paras: Various half courses dealing with special topics; one or more of these will be offered each year as announced by the Department.
Prereq: At least one half course in ethics.

courses.label: PHIL 422
courses.title: Political Philosophy 1
paras: Philosophical analysis of central concepts in political theory and its relation to moral and metaphysical problems of various periods. Prereq: At least one half course in
_ ethics.

courses.label: PHIL 423
courses.title: Political Philosophy 2
paras: A detailed discussion of contemporary theories.
Prereq: At least one half course in ethics.

courses.label: PHIL 425
courses.title: Philosophy of the City
paras: Analysis and evaluation of the philosophical points of view that underlie current criticism of urban life and prevalent schemes for its reconstruction.
Prereq: One half Philosophy course.

courses.label: PHIL 435
courses.title: Studies in Philosophy of Religion
paras: A study of a particular philosopher or problem. The topic witl be announced in advance each year.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 440
courses.title: Logical Theory
paras: A rigorous and General-development o' the propositional and predicate calculus within which alternative calculi are examined. Study of such concepts as completeness, consistency, extensionality, and modality from both formal and philosophical points of view. Intended primarily for those interested in philosophical issues connected with logic. . Prereq: At least one half course in formal logic, 6» consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 440A
courses.title: Logical Theory
paras: The first part of PHIL 440.

courses.label: PHIL 440B
courses.title: Logical Theory
paras: The second part of PHIL 440.

courses.label: PHIL 441
courses.title: Studies In Logic
paras: Various half courses dealing with specific topics; one or more of these will be offered sach year as announced by the Department.
Prereq: PHIL 240, 241, 242, 440A/440B or PMATH 430A.

courses.label: PHIL 446
courses.title: Philosophy of History
paras: Consideration of various possible views about ultimate nature of history and historical knowledge.
Prereq: One full course equivalent in Philosophy, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 455
courses.title: Metaphysics
paras: Studies of reality, metaphysical problems and issues. The first part ontology (nature of being) considers objects, their properties, and causation. The second part cosmology (principles of the universe) examines space, time. and motion.

courses.label: PHIL 455A
courses.title: Ontology
paras: The first part of PHIL 455.

courses.label: PHIL 455B
courses.title: Cosmology
paras: The second part of PHIL 455.
Note Either PHIL 455A or PHIL 455B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 463
courses.title: Philosophy of Language and Linguistic Analysis
paras: The first part examines issues in the philosophy of language, such as synonymy, propasitions, meaning, semantics, reference. The second part will consider ordinary language analysis as a method for solving philosophical problems as compared with structural linguistics.
Prereq: At least one full course equivalent in Philosophy or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 463A
courses.title: Philosophy of Language
paras: The first part of PHIL 363.

courses.label: PHIL 463B
courses.title: Linguistic Analysis
paras: The second part of PHIL 363.
Note Either PHIL 463A or Phil 463B may be taken separately.

courses.label: PHIL 465
courses.title: Existential Philosophy
paras: An in depth study of the thoughts. of a major figure such as Kierkegaard, Unamuno, Nietzsche, Heidegger, Sartre, Camus, Marce Jaspers, Ortega y Gasset.
Prereq: Consent of Instructor

Philosophy

courses.label: PHIL 470
courses.title: Phenomenology
paras: A critical examination of the issues and methods of phenomenology, including the attempt to understand the uses and ramifications of phenomenologicat methods through the working out of particular analyses. The basic writings of phenomenologists such as Husser! and Merieau-Ponty will be used. Prereq: One tull or two half courses in Philosophy, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 471
courses.title: Special Subjects
paras: One or more half courses will be offered at different times, as announced by the Department.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 498
courses.title: Directed Reading in Special Areas
paras: Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 499
courses.title: Senior Seminar and Honours Essay
paras: All senior honours students attend this seminar in which a selection of major philosophical problems is discussed. They will also prepare a senior essay and discuss it with this group.
The following courses are administered by St. Jerome’s College.
PHIL 100) Y.M 3C 1.0" Introduction to Philosophy

A broad selection of the main problems in philosophy wit! be considered. For example: how can we know whether anything is right or wrong? How can we know about things we cannot directly observe? Can we know whether there is a God? Is mind in any sense distinct from matter? ‘

courses.label: PHIL 120J
courses.title: Philosophy of Life and Death
paras: A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the meaning of life and death and the transition from life to death. Students are urged to raise questions and help direct discussion.
Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 130J
courses.title: Philosophy of Discontent
paras: A study of what some of the great philosophers have said about the causes of discontent. Social disobedience and the extent to which
ethical principles can be altered to accommodate changing conditions are possible topics for discussion.
Offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 200J
courses.title: Intentional Logic
paras: An introduction to the understanding of how words are used, the formation of propositions, the construction of arguments and the examination of fallacies to help the student to argue with order, with facility and without error.

courses.label: PHIL 205J
courses.title: Philosophy of Nature
paras: An examination of ancient and modern accounts of the natural worid. Problems include whether matter alone can account for change, whether there is more than one cause, whether nature operates by purpose or chance.
PHIL 206) W 3C 0.5
Philosophy of Science
A philosophical study of the approaches to the material world used by contemporary physical science. The nature and the value of the
experimental method in the writings of scientists past and present will be examined.

courses.label: PHIL 210J
courses.title: Philosophy of Man
paras: What is man? What is man’s place among other creatures? Is man an accident of evolution? What are the
major views on man as a species? How
are love and sex aspects of man's life?

courses.label: PHIL 218J
courses.title: Ethical Theory
paras: A normative approach, employing several of the classic Western traditions of rational thought, to general ethics. The various schools of ethical thought will be discussed.
Also offered in the evening.
PHIL 219) WA 3C 05
Practical Ethics
This course will discuss the applications of general ethics to more specific areas
_ of human endeavour. Among the topics
discussed will be abortion, contraception, sex, obscenity, violence, drugs, egoism, dishonesty, and various forms of human exploitation.
Also offered in the evening.

courses.label: PHIL 230J
courses.title: God and Philosophy
paras: An investigation of several aspects concerning the meaning and existence of God. Is God-taik possible? Can faith and reason be reconciled? ts religious experience a meaningful argument? A wide range of different views will be considered.
PHIL 237J Ethics and Society Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PHIL 260J
courses.title: Issues In Higher Education
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PHIL 300J
courses.title: The Western Philosophical Tradition (to
paras: An intensive overview of the major recurring themes in Western intellectual history from both an historical and a philosophical! viewpoint.
Prereq: Second year standing.
PHIL 301) W 3C 05
The Western Philosophical Tradition (1600-Present)
A continuation of 300J. Descartes to Existentialism.
Prereq: Second year standing.
PHIL 318) W 3C 05
Philosophy of the Family

A philosophical examination of the tamily: its foundation, its purpose, its importance in personal growth and its relation to political community. Prereq: One course in moral philosophy, or consent of instructor.
PHIL 333) Y 3C 1.0 Contemporary Philosophical Problems in Art

An examination of some of the many philosophical problems, especially in music, painting, and poetry, which confront today’s artist as well as his audience. Traditional aesthetic categories are re-evaluated and contemporary philosophies of art considered.
Prereq: One other philosophy course or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 395J
courses.title: The Thomistic Tradition in Philosophy
paras: An examination of the work of Thomas Aquinas, his philosophical relation to his time, the revival of Thomism in the modern era.
Prereq: One full course in philosophy and third year standing, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PHIL 450J
courses.title: Being and Existence
paras: An advanced course for the serious student, delving into the notions of reality, being, essence, existence, analogy, etc. The techniques of linguistic analysis will be employed. Also, the very possibility of any kind of metaphysics will be discussed.
Prereq: Third year standing or consent of instructor.

Course Descriptions
Physics
Physics

courses.label: PHYS 001
courses.title: Pre-University Physics
paras: This course covers the topics in Ontario Grades 11 to 13 essential for first year university physics. The course includes mechanics, gravitation,-vibrations and waves, heat, electricity, light and optics. Successful completion of this course fulfills the University admission requirements where high school Physics is necessary.
No University Credit.
(Offered by Correspondence only)

courses.label: PHYS 010
courses.title: Physics Seminar
paras: This seminar. brings together Honours Physics (including Co-op students) in Years 2,3 and 4, to receive information concerning the activities of the Physics Department and to hear invited speakers.

courses.label: PHYS 103
courses.title: Mechanics in Human Movement
paras: An introduction to the physical principles required for the analysis of the mechanics of human movement. A course for Kinesiology students. Lab alternate weeks, optional tut.

courses.label: PHYS 105
courses.title: Electrical Science
paras: Basic electricity, magnetism and electronics. An introduction to the physica! principles required for an understanding of the electrical instruments used in Kinesiology. A course for Kinesiology students. Prereq: PHYS 103 or 104. Lab alternate weeks, optional tut.

courses.label: PHYS 111
courses.title: Physics For the Life Sciences 1
paras: An introduction to physics for students intending to concentrate their further studies in biology, medicine or dentistry; includes particle kinematics and dynamics, energy and momentum conservation, gravitation, rotational mechanics, fluid mechanics, elasticity and oscillations.

courses.label: PHYS 111L
courses.title: Physics For The Life Sclences 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 111. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 112
courses.title: Physics For The Life Sciences 2
paras: A continuation of PHYS 111; includes wave motion, normal modes of vibration, sound, hearing, temperature, heat, kinetic theory of gases, thermodynamics, electrostatic force and potential electric current and power, OC circuits, magnetic fields and induction.

courses.label: PHYS 112L
courses.title: Physics For The Life Sciences 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 112. Lab alternative weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 115
courses.title: Mechanics
paras: Brief review of kinematics. Particle dynamics, work, energy, conservation of energy. Conservation of linear momentum, collisions. Rotational kinematics and dynamics, conservation of angular momentum. Equilibrium of rigid bodies. For students in Year 1 Engineering.

courses.label: PHYS 121
courses.title: Introductory Physics 1
paras: An introductory course in physics for students intending to concentrate their future studies in the physical sciences, optometry or mathematics; includes particle kinematics and dynamics, forces in nature, work and energy, conservation of energy and linear momentum, rotational kinematics and dynamics, and conservation of angular momentum.
Prereq: Ontario Grade 13 Mathematics. Functions and Relations, and Calculus. Ontario Grade 13 Physics recommended. Science students must take 127L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 121L
courses.title: Introductory Physics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 121. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 122
courses.title: Introductory Physics 2
paras: This course is a continuation of PHYS 121; includes fiuid statics and dynamics, oscillating systems, gravitation, electrical currents and resistive circuits, capacitative and inductive circuits, alternating currents and resonant circuits.
Prereq: PHYS 121. Science students must take 122L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 125
courses.title: Physics for Engineers
paras: Oscillations: simple harmonic motion. Wave motion: travelling and standing waves; transverse and longitudinal waves, including sound. Geometrical optics; reflection and refraction; Physical optics: interference and diffraction. Quantum physics: quantization of radiation; hydrogen atom.

courses.label: PHYS 122L
courses.title: Introductory Physics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 122. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 162
courses.title: Enriched Introductory Physics 1
paras: This is an enriched version of PHYS 121; includes the topics listed in the description of PHYS 121 plus enrichment topics, e.g. Taylor series, numerical methods for solving differential equations and programing the Physics Nova computer.
Prereq: At least 85% average in Ontario Grade 13 Physics, Math-Functions and Relations, and Calculus. Enrolment may be limited. Science students must take 162L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 162L
courses.title: Enriched Introductory Physics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 162.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 163
courses.title: Enriched Introductory Physics 2
paras: This course is a’continuation of PHYS 162; includes topics listed in the description of PHYS 122 plus enrichment topics, e.g. Fourier series, complex exponentials.
Prereq: PHYS 162. Science students must take 163L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 163L
courses.title: Enriched introductory Physics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 163 Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 222
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 1
paras: Not offered 1982-83.
Note.
Students requiring PHYS 222-223 should take PHYS 250 (Fali) and PHYS 243 (Winter).

paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PHYS 223L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism 2 Laboratory

courses.label: PHYS 226
courses.title: Optics 1
paras: Reflection and refraction at plane and curved surfaces, thin and thick lenses, optical instruments.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus. Not for Hons. Physics students. Physics Majors must take PHYS 226L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 226L
courses.title: Optics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 226. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 227
courses.title: Optics 2
paras: The wave nature of light, interference, diffraction, slits and gratings resolution, polarization, photometry, colour. Prereq: PHYS 226. Not for Hons. Physics students. Physics Majors must take PHYS 227L with this course.

courses.label: PHYS 227L
courses.title: Optics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 227. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 243
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electric & magnetic fields, capacitance & dielectrics, electromagnetic induction, instruments, Magnetic properties of matter.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus. This course is primarily intended for Hons. Chem students.

courses.label: PHYS 243L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 243.
Lab. alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 246
courses.title: Physical Optics
paras: Nature of light, wave motion, superposition of waves. Interference of light, Fraunhofer diffraction and resolution limit of optical instruments; the diffraction grating and the analysis of light. Fresnel diffraction. Polarized light. Coherence of light, lasers, holography. Fibre Optics.
Prereq: First year Physics and calculus. Coreq: PHYS 246L. This course is primarily intended for students interested in the Optometry program.

courses.label: PHYS 246L
courses.title: Physical Optics Laboratory
paras: For students taking Phys 246.
- Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 250
courses.title: The Solar System
paras: An introduction to the astronomy and astrophysics of the solar system for students with a background in (elementary) University Physics and Mathematics.
Prereq: First year PHYS and MATH.

courses.label: PHYS 251
courses.title: The Stellar System
paras: An introduction to the astronomy and astrophysics of objects beyond the solar system for students with a background in (elementary) University Physics and Mathematics.
Prereq: First year PHYS and MATH.

courses.label: PHYS 253
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: An introductory course in electricity and magnetism; includes Coulomb's Law, electric fields, Gauss’ Law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, magnetic forces and fields, inductance, magnetization, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves.

Prereq: First year Physics and calculus, MATH 216. Physics majors must take 253L with this course. Recommended for students in Honours programs, This course forms a basis for the understanding of most of today’s electronic and electrical technology.

courses.label: PHYS 253L
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 253.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 254
courses.title: Thermal Physics and Properties of Matter
paras: An introductory course in thermal physics, kinetic theory and properties of matter; includes thermodynamics, heat engines, kinetic theory of gases; viscosity, diffusion, transport properties elasticity.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus. Recommended for students in Honours programs.

courses.label: PHYS 256
courses.title: Wave Motion and Optics
paras: Matrix treatment of ray tracing and wave propagation, cardinal points of optical systems, reflection and transmission coefficients. Coupled oscillators and normal modes, continuous systems and standing waves, Superposition and Fourier analysis, dispersion. Travelling waves and the wave equation. Interference and diffraction.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus. Physics majors must take 256L with this course. Recommended for students in Honours programs.

courses.label: PHYS 256L
courses.title: Optics Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 256. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 259
courses.title: Crystallography and X-Ray Diffraction
paras: Space lattices, symmetry, crystal structure, crystal geometry and stereographic projections. Electronic structure of atoms and atomic bonding in solids. Theory of X-ray diffraction, X-ray methods and the reciprocal lattice. Crystal formation, crystat defects and physical properties of crystals.
Prereq: First year physics and calculus. Coreg: PHYS 259L.

courses.label: PHYS 259L
courses.title: Crystallography and X-Ray Diffraction Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 259.
Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 263
courses.title: Classical Mechanics and Special
paras: Relativity : . Newtonian dynamics of particles and systems of particles; Lagrangian dynamics and generalized coordinates; the Lorentz transformation and relativistic dynamics.

Physics

courses.label: PHYS 270
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in optics and properties of matter, for students taking PHYS 256L.
Lab. alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 271
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in electricity, magnetism and properties of matter, for students taking PHYS 253L.

courses.label: PHYS 301
courses.title: Physical Techniques for Biologists 1
paras: Visible, UV, dark field, phase, interference, polarizing and fluorescence microscopy; electron microscopy; visible and UV spectroscopy; polarography; pH and ion electrodes; osmometers; densitometers; radioactive tracers and counters; introductory electronics; data analysis. Offered alternate years with PHYS 302. Prereq: First year physics. Physics students may not take this course for credit..

courses.label: PHYS 302
courses.title: Physical Techniques for Biologist 2 Infrared, Roman and fluorescence
paras: spectroscopy; nuclear magnetic and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy; optical rotary dispersion and circular dichroism; X-ray diffraction; chromatography and electrophoresis; differential scanning calorimetry; ultra centrifugation; flame photometry; X-ray and atomic absorption spectroscopy; cell counting, cytofluorometry and cell viability. Offered alternate years with PHYS 301. Prereq: First year physics. Physics students may not take this course for credit.

courses.label: PHYS 324
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics 1
paras: Fundamentals of modern physics, special theory of relativity, quantization of electromagnetic radiation, wave properties of particles, the hydrogen atom.
Prereq: PHYS 222, 223, 226 and 227. Recommended for students in General programs.

courses.label: PHYS 325
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics 2
paras: Many electron atoms, atomic and X-ray spectra, nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, molecular and solid state physics.
Prereq: PHYS 324. Recommended for students in General programs.

courses.label: PHYS 350
courses.title: Astrophysics 1
paras: Atomic and molecular spectra, forbidden and permitted transitions. Emission and absorption of radiation. Planck, Saha and Boltzmann equations. Line broadening effects. Radiation transfer theory. Sources of opacity. The spectra of the sun and stars. ~
Prereq: None, however familiarity with the contents of PHYS 250-251 will be assumed. For third and fourth year students.

courses.label: PHYS 351
courses.title: Astrophysics 2
paras: Physical properties of the stars. Stellar distance determination. Distribution of the stars in space. The solar motion. Galactic rotation. Stellar dynamics. Characteristics and structure of our galaxy and external systems.
Prereq: None, however, familiarity with the contents of PHYS 250-251 will be assumed. For third and fourth year students.
Note
PHYS 449, PHYS 451, are also open to third and fourth year students. PHYS 350 alternates with PHYS 451 and PHYS 351 alternates with PHYS 449.

courses.label: PHYS 352
courses.title: Electronics 1
paras: DC and AC circuit theory, p and n materials, pn diodes junction and FET transistors. Transistor amplifiers and their equivalent circuits. Operational amplifiers. Feedback, oscillators and power supplies.
Prereq: Knowledge of determinants, elementary calculus and elementary electricity.
Coreq: 352L

courses.label: PHYS 352L
courses.title: Electronics 1 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 352. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 353
courses.title: Electronics 2
paras: Logic gates, flip-flops and shift registers. Binary numbers and Boolean algebra. An introduction to microprocessors is discussed based on the 6800. This will include arithmetic logic units, parallel input/output ports, assembly language and a number of examples.
Prereq: PHYS 352 or equivalent. Coreq: PHYS 353L.

courses.label: PHYS 353L
courses.title: Electronics 2 Laboratory
paras: For students taking PHYS 353. Lab alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 354
courses.title: Atomic and Molecular Physics
paras: The Schrédinger equation applied to simple one-and three-dimension potentials, hydrogen atoms, angular momentum and spin, molecular vibrations and rotations, many electron atoms, radiation processes.
Prereq: PHYS 263

courses.label: PHYS 358
courses.title: Thermodynamics
paras: Thermodynamic systems, equation of state, the laws of thermodynamics with applications. Change of phase. , Prereq: MATH 213a-213b and a first year physics course.

courses.label: PHYS 359
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Basic theory. Ideal classical and quantum gas. Occupation numbers. Effects of statistics. Applications to metals, perfect crystals, radiation and dense fluids.
Prereq: PHYS 358

courses.label: PHYS 360A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in mechanics, atomic physics, solid state physics, optics and electronics.
18 hours of experiments

courses.label: PHYS 360B
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Continuation of 360A.
18 hours of experiments

courses.label: PHYS 363
courses.title: Classicat Mechanics
paras: Application of the methods of classicai mechanics to central force motion, rigid body rotation, coupled oscillations and motion in non-inertial frames; survey of Hamiltonian: dynamics.
Prereq: PHYS 263. This course is primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 364
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 1
paras: Vector analysis and applications. Vector operators using curvilinear coordinates. Cartesian tensors. Inertia tensor; stress, strain and rate of strain tensors.

Physics
Applications to elasticity, fluids, electromagnetism and relativity. Prereg: MATH 213a-213b and 216. This course is primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 365
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 2
paras: Fourier series, integral and transform with applications. Use of the Laplace transform in physics. Partial differential equations of mathematical physics. Separation of variables. Besse! and Legendre functions with application. Sturm-Liouville theory. Other special functions.
Prereq: MATH 213a-213b and 216. This course is primarily intended for Honours Physics students.

courses.label: PHYS 368
courses.title: Geophysics 1
paras: Introductory topics on the physics of
the earth. Seismology and the earth's interior. Thermal history of the earth, gravity and isostasy. Origin of the continents and continental! drift. {Identical to EARTH 368).
Prereq: First year physics and calculus.

courses.label: PHYS 369
courses.title: Geophysics 2
paras: The geology of the ocean basins. Topics in physical oceanography. Physical properties of ocean water, heat budget of the world oceans. Oceanic circulations. Coriolis effects. Some idealized current regimes. (Identical to EARTH 389).
Prereq: First year physics and calculus.

courses.label: PHYS 371A
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Further experiments in atomic, nuctear and solid state physics, optics and electronics. For honours students who are taking PHYS 360A.
18 hours experiments.

courses.label: PHYS 371B
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Continuation of 371A.
For honours students who are taking Phys 360B.
18 hours experiments.

courses.label: PHYS 380
courses.title: Molecular Biophysics
paras: Macromolecular structure and function, weak interactions, DNA replication, protein synthesis, energy production, photosynthesis, contro! of intracellular processes, structure of viruses, physical techniques.

courses.label: PHYS 381
courses.title: Celt Biophysics
paras: Structure and function of cellular membranes and organelies, membrane potentials and ion transport, nerve conduction, muscle contraction, vision and interaction of light with cells intercellular communication, growth control.

courses.label: PHYS 432
courses.title: Physics of Solid State Devices
paras: The theories of solid state physics are applied to explain the operation and use of several modern electronic devices, including the p-n junction, transistors, thyristors, tunnel diodes, field effect devices, optical devices, etc.
Prereq: PHYS 435

courses.label: PHYS 433
courses.title: Experimental Research Project
paras: An experimental research project. This course is designed for students in the Honours Physics program and in the Cooperative Applied Physics program. Students in the reguiar Hons Physics program must take either PHYS 433 or PHYS 437. Although students in the Cooperative Applied Physics (Hons) program are recommended to take one of these courses, enrolment may be limited.

courses.label: PHYS 434
courses.title: Introductory Quantum Mechanics
paras: Origins and necessity for quantum mechanics and its concepts and formulation. The Hamiltonian operator and Schrédinger's equation, the harmonic oscillator (Schrddinger’'s treatment). The uncertainty principle. Momentum representation. One dimensional potential problems. Angular momentum. The hydrogen atom. Prereq: PHYS 354.

courses.label: PHYS 435
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Introductory concepts in crystal diffraction and the reciprocal lattice. Crystal bonding, tattice vibrations, thermal properties of insulators, free-electron theory of metals, band theory, semiconductors.
Prereq: PHYS 263.

courses.label: PHYS 437A
courses.title: Theoretical Physics Project
paras: Selected subjects for advanced study by theoretically inclined students, topics in relativistic, quantum, and siatistical physics. Fall term enrolment will be limited.

Students in the regular Hons Physics program must take either PHYS 437A or PHYS 433. Although students in the Cooperative Applied Physics (Hons) program are encouraged to take one of these courses, enroiment may be limited.

courses.label: PHYS 497B
courses.title: Continued Theoretical Physics Project
paras: Acontinuation and extension of the Project initiated in PHYS 437A. Available only to those students who have satisfactorily completed that portion of the project contained in PHYS 437A in the immediately preceeding term.
Note

Students intending to take both PHYS 437A and 437B must register for both courses, and have their registration - approved by the Theoretical Physics Project co-ordinator, at the start of the Fall term.

courses.label: PHYS 441
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory
paras: A generalized treatment of the basic laws of electricity and magnetism, mathematical techniques for the problems of electrostatics, solution of Maxwell's equations in free space and the study of plane waves, theory of waveguides and introduction to radiation.
Prereq: PHYS 222-223 or PHYS 253, PHYS 364-365.

courses.label: PHYS 442
courses.title: Structure of Solids
paras: A survey with emphasis on the physical properties and behaviour of metals and alloys. Elastic and plastic deformations of crystals. Solidification, structure of alloys, free energy of alloy systems, equilibrium diagrams, diffusion, solid state phase transformations.
Prereq: PHYS 435

courses.label: PHYS 443
courses.title: Continuum Mechanics
paras: General description of continuum behaviour: stress, strain, rate of strain, constitutive relations, equations of motion, effect of symmetry, thermodynamics. Elastic media: Hooke's law, simple problems, elastic waves. Fluids: classification, perfect fluids. Newtonian fluids, boundary layers, turbulence. Viscoelasticity, plastoelasticity. Applications to various systems. ‘
Prereq: PHYS 364-365.
Course Descriptions
Physics .

courses.label: PHYS 444
courses.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
paras: Theory of deuteron. Nucleon-nucleon scattering. Nuclear models. Basic concepts in particle physics. Conservation taws and invariance principles. SU (3) model. The quark model.
Prereq: PHYS 455, and PHYS 434

courses.label: PHYS 445
courses.title: Modern Optics
paras: Basic electromagnetic wave theory. Polarization reflection, refraction and dispersion. Fibre optics and communications. Temporal coherence and spectra. Spatial coherence and diffraction. Phase contrast microscopy. Basics of Holography. Crystal optics and nonlinear effects. Lasers, modes, pulses and propagation of beams. Prereq: PHYS 256 and PHYS 354.

courses.label: PHYS 449
courses.title: Radio Astronomy
paras: Radio telescopes. Radio sources including the sun. H II regions, H | regions. The galactic centre, pulsars, quasars, other extragalactic sources, cosmological implications.
Prereq: PHYS 223 and PHYS 250-251

courses.label: PHYS 450
courses.title: Astrophysics 3
paras: Solar system astrophysics (excluding the sun). The physical nature of planetary (and satellite) surfaces, atmospheres and interiors. Asteroids, meteorites and comets. The interplanetary medium (solar wind). Solar interactions with the interplanetary medium and earth's magnetosphere.
Prereq: none, however, familiarity with
the contents of PHYS 250-251 will be assumed.

courses.label: PHYS 451
courses.title: Astrophysics 4
paras: The structure of stellar interiors, nuclear reactions and energy sources inlthe stars of the main sequence, early evolution of stars from the main sequence. Lifetimes of the stars.
Prereq: None, however, familiarity with the contents of PHYS 250-251 will be assumed.
Note
PHYS 350, PHYS 351 are also open to third and fourth year students. PHYS 350 and PHYS 351 are offered in alternate years to PHYS 449 and PHYS 451.

courses.label: PHYS 453
courses.title: Electronics 4
paras: A variety of topics in the operation of systems. Transistors, modern circuit techniques, noise, stability under feedback, information theory, and possible student motivated topics. Inctudes laboratory demonstrations.
Prereq: PHYS 352-353

courses.label: PHYS 454
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
paras: The matrix formulation of quantum mechanics. The harmonic oscillator (Heisenberg’s treatment). The matrices for angular momentum. Time-independent and time-dependent perturbation theory. The interaction of atomic systems with radiation. Multiparticte systems, identical particles. Pauli exclusion principle. The helium atom. Prereq: PHYS 434.
Note PHYS 454 is strongly recommended for Students intending to do graduate work.

courses.label: PHYS 455
courses.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
paras: Nuclear structure, interactions of nuclear radiations with matter, radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, nuclear force, elementary particles.
Prereq: PHYS 354.

courses.label: PHYS 464
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 3
paras: Applications to Physics of the theory of functions of a complex variable. Prereq: PHYS 364-365.

courses.label: PHYS 465
courses.title: Mathematical Physics 4
paras: Theory and applications of integral transforms, integral equations and Green's functions. Numerical Methods. Prereq: PHYS 464

courses.label: PHYS 480
courses.title: Radiation Biophysics
paras: The effect of radiation of various kinds on cells and tissues, exposure calculations, mechanism of damage, repair theories, genetic effect, target theory, isotopic tracers in biophysical research.

courses.label: PHYS 481
courses.title: Biophysics of Organ Systems
paras: Physics of hemeostasis, interactions with the environment, circulation of blood, temperature regulation, respiration, transport problems and special organ systems.

courses.label: PHYS 482
courses.title: Biophysics of Nervous Systems
paras: Neurons; nerve conduction, sensory transducers; coding, processing and storage of information; control of muscles and other effector organs. Recommended for third or fourth year students in Math, Eng, Sci or HKLS.
