courses.label: PSCI 101
courses.title: Introduction to Politics 1
paras: An introduction to the nature of politics and to the conflict of modern political ideas. The course involves a common lecture series and tutorials led by faculty members.
Note
P SCI 102 consists of a series of courses dealing with different aspects of politics. Students should select the course which most closely corresponds to their interests.

courses.label: PSCI 102A
courses.title: Imperialism in International Relations
paras: A discussion of the idea of imperialism in ancient and modern international relations, the causes and motives of imperialism, changes in imperial strategies, and the difference between the ‘old’ and the ‘new’ imperialism.

courses.label: PSCI 102C
courses.title: Politics in Action
paras: An examination of the way in which society's conflicting demands are organized, articulated, and translated in action. The part played by the various political and economic forces in society will be examined in a comparative framework.

courses.label: PSCI 102D
courses.title: The Political Process in the Modern Democracies
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 102E
courses.title: Political Rights and Obligations
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 102F
courses.title: Populist Politics in the Third World
paras: The course examines worker and peasant protest movements in the Third World with emphasis on Africa and Latin America. Students will study the ideas, appeal and leadership of selected Third World movements and parties, focusing upon the social and economic conditions which gave rise to them.

courses.label: PSCI 102H
courses.title: Citizen Participation in Canada
paras: An investigation of the relationship between political participation and democracy - exploring the question of how much participation is good and the ways in which it can be exercised - leading to an in-depth examination of the distribution of power in Canada.

courses.label: PSCI 102K
courses.title: Mass Political Violence
paras: A distinctive social feature of our century is the amount of political violence. Man-made deaths number approximately one hundred-million. This course will describe and evaluate various theories of political violence.

courses.label: PSCI 102L
courses.title: Political Influence in Ontario
paras: An introductory description of the political process in Ontario, based ona case study of the steps taken by a Particular interest group to obtain legislative recognition of their demands in the field of local government.
PSCItH 102M W,S 0.5
Contemporary Issues in Canadian Public Policy
An evaluation of various public policy responses to some contemporary Canadian social, cultural, economic, environmental, and political problems, as well as the process of policy-making.

courses.label: PSCI 214
courses.title: Quantitative Analysis
paras: An introduction to the use of quantitative methods in Political Science. Only a rudimentary understanding of mathematics is required.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 225
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 1
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of Western political theorists from the earliest times to the seventeenth century.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 226
courses.title: The History of Political Theory 2
paras: A survey of the principal ideas of Western political theorists since the seventeenth century.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 253
courses.title: Comparative Communism 1
paras: An examination of the historical development of the communist international system, the cause of its diversity and doctrinal variety, with emphasis on common problems and the role of ruling parties, their objectives, performance, and strategy.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 254
courses.title: Comparative Communism 2
paras: This course will concentrate on contemporary issues in communist politics, examining selected ruling and non-ruling communist parties.
Prereq: P SCI 253 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 255
courses.title: The Politics of Western Industrial Nations
paras: A systematic introduction to the political processes of industrial countries. The central focus will be on Western Europe and North America. Some attention, however, will be devoted to the Antipodes, the Mediterranean countries, South Africa and Japan.
Prereq: Second year standing.

courses.label: PSCI 260A
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics 1
paras: An analysis of the political environment in which the Canadian political system operates, including discussion of the Canadian political culture, federalism, the constitution, federat-provincial relations, and the role of the Governor General.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 260B
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics 2
paras: An analysis of the decision-making machinery of the Canadian political system, including discussion of cabinet government, the role of the House of Commons, interest groups, the electoral system, the party system and voting behaviour.
Prereq: P SCI 260A or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 264
courses.title: American Government and Politics
paras: The theory and practice of the American political system as revealed
Course Descriptions
Political Science
by the institutions and operations of American national government.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 268
courses.title: British Government and Politics
paras: An examination of the uniquely British characteristics of the British political system.
No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 271
courses.title: Political Behaviour 1
paras: Empirical approaches to the study of politics are examined in light of their assumptions, aspirations, and critics. No prereq for students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 272
courses.title: Political Behaviour 2
paras: An examination of the political attitudes and behaviour of men and women in different political systems.
Prereq: P SCI 271 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 281
courses.title: Internationat Politics
paras: This course studies the transformation of the international! system stressing East-West, Rich-Poor, and North-South perspectives and interactions.
No preregq for students in the second year and above.
PSC! 282 W 2C 05
Foreign Policy
This course studies the roots of foreign policy behaviour of selected western and non-western (particularly Asian) states.
Prereq: P SC! 281 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 291
courses.title: The Canadian Legal Process
paras: An analysis of the manner in which the Common Law functions, together with an examination of the structure and jurisdiction of the Canadian court systems. Taught by a member of the legal profession.
Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 292
courses.title: Issues in Canadian Criminal Law
paras: Rational! principles and concepts applicable to current emotional criminal

issues are analysed by a practising crown attorney, for example, abortion, euthanasia, pornography, seat belts, homosexuality, marijuana, police power, civil rights, criminal trials, jury, capital punishment, prisons, etc. Prereq: Open to all students in the second year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 311
courses.title: Methodology of Political Science: The Foundations
paras: A selective examination of seminal works which have contributed to our understanding of the methods appropriate to the study of politics. Not a survey course.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 312
courses.title: Approaches to Survey Analysis in Political Science
paras: This course introduces students with previous experience in statistical methods to the special problems associated with the analysis of the nominal data collected in surveys. Prereq: P SC! 214

courses.label: PSCI 315
courses.title: Research Design in Political Science
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 321
courses.title: Marxist Theory
paras: An examination of the formation of Marx's method and of its significance for the proletariat.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 322
courses.title: Marxism and Revolution After Marx
paras: A selective study of developments in Marxist theory and political movements after Marx.
Prereq: P SCi 321

courses.label: PSCI 323
courses.title: Ancient Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of political philosophy during the classical period in Greece.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 324
courses.title: Modern Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of political philosophy in the modern period. Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 325
courses.title: Radical Political Theory
paras: A discussion of non-marxian political ideas such as social gospel, populism, fascism and Fabian socialism; and their socio-economic roots and sources. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 327
courses.title: Political Science and Political Values
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 331
courses.title: Public Administration 1
paras: An introduction to the principles of
public administration illustrated by the ©
study of Canadian institutions largely at the federal level, but including provincial and municipal examples. Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 332
courses.title: Public Administration 2
paras: Analyses of problems and issues in the field applying the knowledge gained in P SC1 331.
Prereq: P SC! 331 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 333
courses.title: Administrative Law
paras: A study of Canadian adminstrative law including the delegation of political power to various administrative agencies which play a prominent role in controlling contemporary social and economic life. The supervisory role of the courts will also be examined. Prereq: P SC! 331 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 341
courses.title: Provincial Politics
paras: A comparative analysis of the political systems of the Canadian provinces which explores the possibility that as many as ten political cultures exist in Canada.
Prereq: P SC! 260A and 2608

courses.label: PSCI 342
courses.title: Politics in Quebec
paras: A seminar dealing with the political and social development of Quebec. The emphasis will be on the problems and issues of contemporary Quebec. Prereq: P SC! 260A and 260B or 341 or consent of instructor.
Course Descriptions 387
Political Science

courses.label: PSCI 343
courses.title: Canadian Municipal Government
paras: A study of the assumptions, structures, and performance of municipal government in Canada with reference to metropolitan and regional structural innovations (particularly in Ontario). Open to students in the third year and above with at least one previous course in Political Science.

courses.label: PSCI 344
courses.title: The Politics of Local Government
paras: A study of the political process in selected Canadian cities focusing on citizen participation, internal decisionmaking, leadership, and the allocation of power.
Prereq: P SC! 343 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 350A
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 1
paras: An introduction to the politics of Asia, Africa and Latin America focusing upon the political impact of world trade, colonization and foreign investment
No preregq for students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 350B
courses.title: The Politics of the Developing Areas 2
paras: An examination of the politics of the developing areas with emphasis on the political behaviour of peasants, the urban poor, organized labour and the military.
No prereg for students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 351
courses.title: Comparative Federal Systems
paras: A comparative examination of federal systems, with an emphasis on the problems and processes of integration and disintegration.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 352
courses.title: Comparative Legislative Systems
paras: A comparison of the institutional and behavioural characteristics of legislatures in a comparative framework, with emphasis on Canada, the United States, Great Britain, and Australia. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 362
courses.title: Soviet Government and Politics
paras: An intensive survey of the development of Soviet political structures with analysis of the relative influence of ideological goais on the one hand and social forces on the other.
Prereq: P SC! 253-254 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 363
courses.title: Canadian Constitutional Law
paras: An introduction to the nature and basic principles of constitutional law. This course will deal especially with the distribution of powers in the Canadian federation, and its evolution, notably by judicial decision. Leading cases will be examined.
Prereq: P SC! 260A and 2608 or 260A and consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 364
courses.title: Politics in Italy
paras: An examination of the social, economic, and ideological forces underlying contemporary politics in Italy.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 371
courses.title: Political Culture
paras: An analysis of the development of the concept of political culture as an analytical tool. . Prereq: P SCI 271/272 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 373
courses.title: Political Parties
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 374
courses.title: Interest Group Politics
paras: A study of interest group theory and comparative analysis of the internal politics of interest groups and their role in the political process.
Prereq: At least one of P SCi 260A and 260B, 264, 268, 271, 272.

courses.label: PSCI 375
courses.title: The Politics of Self-Management
paras: An examination of the participation of citizens in decision making, both at work and in politics. The selfmanagement system of Yugoslavia wil! be studied in detail.
Prereq: Second year standing or above.

courses.label: PSCI 380A
courses.title: World Politics 1
paras: An examination of the structure of the world capitalist system concentrating upon warfare between core states during 1815-1945 and assessing the impact of the nuclear revolution. A number of classic theories of imperialism are considered.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 380B
courses.title: World Politics 2
paras: An examination of the allocation of misery in the world capitalist system. The focus is on core/periphery relations and a number of theories of imperialism are considered.
Open only to students in the third year and above.

courses.label: PSCI 390
courses.title: Special Studies
paras: From time to time courses of special study may be added to the program at the third year level. Students wishing to take such courses should consult the Department's Undergraduate Officer.

courses.label: PSCI 411
courses.title: Theories and Methods of Political Science
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 424
courses.title: Contemporary Socialist and Communist Thought
paras: This course examines recent trends in Marxist theory and its contribution to the analysis of capitalist and socialist societies.
Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 425
courses.title: English Political Theory of the Nineteenth Century
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 426
courses.title: Selected Subjects in Political Philosophy
paras: A selective treatment of basic themes in political philosophy in the modern and pre-modern periods.
For third year Political Science students, but open to others with prereq P SCI 221, 222, 323, or 324, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 427
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Philosophy
paras: A selective examination of basic problems in political philosophy in the modern and pre-modern periods. Prereq: P SCI 221, 222, 323 or 324.

courses.label: PSCI 428
courses.title: State and Economic Life
paras: An analytical and comparative study of the growth of government intervention in the economic process, and of the development of the welfare state. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 431
courses.title: Canadian Public Policy
paras: An examination of the way that policymaking processes and institutions have responded to the problems of governing in the postwar period. The focus will be on policies regarding the policy-making process itself.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 260B and consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 435
courses.title: The Politics of Canadian Resource Development
paras: A seminar focusing on the strategies of resource development policies, with an emphasis on the economic, political, environmental and cultural implications of oil, natural gas, and mineral exploitation.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor..

courses.label: PSCI 436
courses.title: Comparative Public Policy
paras: A comparative examination of public policy and approaches to the study of public policy, with case studies from Germany, Britain, France, Sweden, Canada, the United States and India. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 437
courses.title: The Politics of International Resources
paras: An examination of the politics of International resources. Attention will be given to the set of issues relating to minerals, water, oceanic fisheries, oil energy, timber and labour.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 438
courses.title: The Canadian Welfare State
paras: A seminar dealing with the rationale, history and present structure of the Canadian weifare state, with special emphasis on income security programs
and policies such as Unemployment insurance, Old Age Security and the Canadian pension system.
Prereq: P SCI 260A and 8; or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 439
courses.title: The Politics of Canadian Economic Policy
paras: A seminar examining the ‘political dimensions of selected economic policy issues such as: foreign ownership and industrial strategy, restraint in government spending, regional development and other matters. Prereg: P SCi 260A and B and ECON 100; or permission of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 442
courses.title: Politics in Ontario
paras: A critical examination of the distinctive elements of government and politics in the Province of Ontario.
Prereq: P SC! 260A and 2608 or 341 or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 443
courses.title: Politics in Western Canada
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 445
courses.title: Politics in the Atlantic Provinces
paras: Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 453
courses.title: Comparative Politics 1
paras: Selected Topics in Comparative Politics Prereg: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 454
courses.title: Comparative Politics II
paras: Selected Topics in Comparative Politics. Prereq: P SCI 453.

courses.label: PSCI 461
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 1
paras: A critical examination of various problems of Canadian politics, with an emphasis on political integration, federalism and political parties. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 462
courses.title: Problems in Canadian Politics 2
paras: A senior research course on selected aspects of Canadian political life, with emphasis on the preparation of a major and original research paper.
For fourth year Political Science Students but open to others with prereq P SCi 461.
“psct471 05 Public Opinion and Propaganda A detailed study of the nature of public opinion and the attempt to contro! it through propaganda. Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 473
courses.title: Voting Behaviour
paras: A comparative study of the motivations underlying electoral choice in Canada, Great Britain and the United States. Prereq: P SCi 214, 373 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 475
courses.title: Political Socialization
paras: A study of the processes and agents of political socialization and their effects on political stability or change in liberaldemocratic societies.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 476
courses.title: Research Seminar in Political Behaviour
paras: A research-oriented seminar on selected theoretical works in political behaviour, with an emphasis on the development of research projects dealing with Canadian topics.
Prereq: Consent of the instructor.
P SCI 479 : Senior Research Seminar: Violence in the Political Process
Not offered 1982-83.

courses.label: PSCI 481
courses.title: Research Seminar on World Politics
paras: Not offered 1982-83..

courses.label: PSCI 483
courses.title: Power Politics and Worid Order Studies
paras: This theory course examines the evolution of the international system.
- the capacity of the system of states to cope with the demands on it; meanings of international and regional power and order..
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 484
courses.title: Contemporary Strategies: Theories and Policies
paras: The course examines strdtegic studies and their premises, the evolution of strategic thinking, the role of national policies of military powers. Strategic concepts are studied with specific reference to military policies of regional powers.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSCI 486
courses.title: Middle Powers and World Politics
paras: The course studies the literature on middle powers (including Canada). Particular emphasis is on the study of self-images, views of power, of power politics, and the sources of influence of these powers.
Prereq: Fourth year standing or consent of the instructor.

courses.label: PSYCH 101
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: A general survey course designed to provide the student with an understanding of the basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science.
Also offered at Renison College and St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 102
courses.title: Introductory Psychology Special Topics
paras: A study in greater depth of selected broad issues anc problems introduced in Psychology 101.
Also offered at Renison College and St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 102A
courses.title: Applied Psychology Applications of Psychotogical research
paras: to contemporary problems: man and en-
vironment, human factors engineering, management and organizations, crime and violence, and public health.

courses.label: PSYCH 102B
courses.title: Nature, Nurture and Human Behaviour
paras: The role of heredity and environment in the development of intelligence, personality and personality disorders, and conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102C
courses.title: Culture’s Influence on Behaviour
paras: The role of culture on the development of Perception, Cognition, Learning, and Memory; Cultural influences on personality and personality disorders, and on conflict and aggression.

courses.label: PSYCH 102D
courses.title: Psychology of Consciousness
paras: Modes of thinking, emotion, creativity, and altered states of consciousness.

courses.label: PSYCH 102E
courses.title: Psychological Intervention Applications of Psychology to human
paras: coping, problems and growth with emphasis on analyzing critically current treatment methods.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 102F
courses.title: Personal Adjustment
paras: Focus on research which investigates the everyday task of coping with ourselves, our environment, and the people we encounter. Topics will focus on the themes of knowing the self, interpersonal relationships, and of the way in which our social and physical environment affects our behaviour.

courses.label: PSYCH 200
courses.title: Measurement in Psychology
paras: The logic of measurement in Psychology. Descriptive procedures for collecting and handling data. Making inferences from test scores. The use of
’ correlational procedures in measuring
intelligence, achievement, aptitudes, interests and personality.

courses.label: PSYCH 201
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Psychology
paras: An introduction to data analysis. Topics covered include descriptive statistics and the logic and methods of inferential statistics with emphasis on applications in psychology: Little mathematics background is assumed.

courses.label: PSYCH 202
courses.title: Experimental Design
paras: An examination of the effective use and interpretation of statistics in design and understanding of experiments in the social sciences.
Prereq: PSYCH 201

courses.label: PSYCH 203
courses.title: Learning and Motivation
paras: This course is designed to introduce the student to theories in Learning and Motivation and to provide the student with an understanding of the experimental techniques in these areas. Prereq: PSYCH 107

courses.label: PSYCH 206
courses.title: Perceptual Processes
paras: An examination of data and theory concerning perceptual processes. Topics will include the perception of form and space, perceptual learning and a consideration of the effect of personality variables in perception. Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 207
courses.title: Cognitive Processes
paras: An examination and evaluation of selected topics dealing with human learning, thinking, concept formation, memory and language.
Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 211
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
paras: An examination of the process and factors of human development. Prereq: PSYCH 101
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 212
courses.title: Educational Psychology
paras: A consideration of the main variables affecting learning in the classroom with special focus upon the conditions
. essential to efficient learning. Prereq: PSYCH 101 Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 213
courses.title: Exceptional Children
paras: Educational problems associated with mental retardation, emotional disturbances, sensory and physica! impairments and intellectual giftedness.

courses.label: PSYCH 214
courses.title: Psychology of Adolescence
paras: A study of the psychological processes in the second decade of human development. Consideration is given to such areas as intellectual, emotional and social growth, and identity formation. Current concepts, issues, and research are stressed.
Prereq: PSYCH 211
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 218
courses.title: Aging, Dying and Death
paras: An examination of the psychological aspects of aging and the traditional and recent literature relating to various views On the reality of death in the life of man. Therapy with dying individuals is reviewed and evaluated.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 231
courses.title: Psychology of Religious Experience
paras: Approaches of traditional psychological theories and especially of a modern psychology of consciousness toward phenomena of religious experience.
mysticism and meditation are examined.
The transcendant phenomena are compared with other altered states of consciousness”
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.
- Course Descriptions 391
Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 236
courses.title: A Psychological Analysis of Human Sexuality ,
paras: (This course will examine psychological and social psychological theories and empirical investigations of human sexuality.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor..
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 253
courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: An introduction to theories and research on people in their physical and social environment. Typically, topics such as conformity, persuasion, attraction, prejudice, communication, aggression, the psychology of freedom, justice and human exchange will be introduced.
Prereq: PSYCH 101, Cross-listed as PSYCH 220R

courses.label: PSYCH 254
courses.title: Interpersonal Relations
paras: A psychological analysis of social interaction. The development of interpersonal attraction from first impressions to long-term relationships. The roots of hostility, conflict and communication problems.
Prereq: PSYCH 253, Cross-listed as: PSYCH 221R

courses.label: PSYCH 258
courses.title: Principles and Evolution of Psychoanalytic Thought
paras: This course expresses the fundamental psychoanalytic vision as articulated by Sigmund Freud, and its relevance to the
. humanities. The theme is to understand
the potentially liberating spirit which is at the root of psychoanalysis.
Prereq: PSYCH 107
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 261
courses.title: Physiological Psychology
paras: Introduction to brain, basic physiological processes and their roles in behaviour. Course covers sensing and perceiving; neural bases of action: motivation; learning and memory; and consciousness. Both experimental and clinical data are considered.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: PSYCH 271
courses.title: Animal Behaviour
paras: Survey of mechanisms, development, adaptive value and evaluation of behaviour in non-human animals. Covers ethology, sociobiology and experimental comparative psychology. Emphasis on principles of research with laboratory and wiid animais as weli as methods of observing behaviour. Prereq: PSYCH 101 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: PSYCH 293
courses.title: Research in Learning and Motivation
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Program (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programs).
Prereq: PSYCH 201 and one of PSYCH 203 or 271.

courses.label: PSYCH 295
courses.title: Research in Perceptual and Cognitive Processes
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Program (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programs).
Prereq: PSYCH 201 and one of PSYCH 206 or 207

courses.label: PSYCH 297
courses.title: Research in Biopsychology
paras: Open only to students in a Psychology Program (Honours, Joint Honours, General or Minor Programs).
Prereq: PSYCH 201 and PSYCH 261

courses.label: PSYCH 301
courses.title: Tests and Measurement
paras: An introduction to the theory and use of psychological tests. Special emphasis is placed on the assessment of personality, intelligence, aptitudes and interests.
Prereq: PSYCH 201

courses.label: PSYCH 305
courses.title: Sensory Processes
paras: A consideration of data and theory concerning sensory processes. Topics will include psychophysical methodology, sensory mechanisms, and the neuropsychological basis of perceptions.
Prereq: PSYCH 206

courses.label: PSYCH 307
courses.title: Cognitive Neurology
paras: An examination of issues related to understanding the cerebral organization of motor skill. Discussion of how certain movement disorders are a reflection of disturbances at different stages in the sequence of information processing. Prereq: One of PSYCH 206, 207, or KIN 356, Cross-listed as KIN 456

courses.label: PSYCH 311
courses.title: Behaviour and Development of Human Infants
paras: The purposes of this course are to study the behaviour and development of human infants, to gain direct experience with infants, and to examine community attitudes and resources available for infant care.
Prereq: PSYCH 211 or permission of instructor.

courses.label: PSYCH 312
courses.title: Learning Disabilities
paras: A critical examination of the concept of learning disability and of current issues in the assessment and remediation of learning problems.
Prereq: PSYCH 211 ar PSYCH 212 or PSYCH 213
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 316
courses.title: Moral Development
paras: A consideration of psychological theory and research dealing withthe nature and origin of moral development, developmental differences in moral judgement, and various approaches to teaching moral behaviour with its consequent effects on the individual. Prereq: PSYCH 271
Oftered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 317
courses.title: The Emotionally Disturbed Child
paras: A review of traditional concepts, current thoughts and major research on the psychopathology of childhood. Specific attention will be given to socialization processes and educational procedures. Prereq: PSYCH 2171
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 322
courses.title: Principles and Practice in Early Childhood Education 1
paras: Current principles of teaching preschool-aged children. An emphasis is placed on those curricula which aim to foster social and cognitive development. Topics include: characteristics and needs of children in group-care settings; classroom management; curriculum planning. Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option
Course Descriptions
Psychology

courses.label: PSYCH 323
courses.title: Practicum in Early Childhood Education
paras: Directed supervision with young children in group settings. The course requires 3 hours of field work per week. Must be taken concurrently with PSYCH 322.
Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option (Honours)

courses.label: PSYCH 325
courses.title: Practicum In Early Childhood Education A
paras: Directed supervision with young children in group settings. The course requires 3 hours of field work per week over two terms. In addition, students are required to complete 4 full-day weeks in block placements during the academic year. Must be taken concurrently with PSYCH 322.
Pass/Fail Grading
Prereq: Acceptance into the Early Childhood Education and Care Option (Genera!)

courses.label: PSYCH 331
courses.title: Individual Differences
paras: An analysis of individual and group differences in behaviour, with emphasis on studies of intelligence.
Prereq: PSYCH 200 or PSYCH 301

courses.label: PSYCH 333
courses.title: Industrial/Organizational Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods and problems in Industrial Psychology. Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 334
courses.title: Theories of Individual Counselling Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods, theories and problems in Individual Counselling Psychology.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Also offered at Renison and St. Jerome's Colleges.

courses.label: PSYCH 335
courses.title: Personality and Behaviour Change
paras: Forms of psychological intervention that produce important changes in the way people think, feel and behave including psychoanalysis, behaviour - therapy, brainwashing, cult conversions, deprogramming, hypnosis, biofeedback and meditation.
Prereq: PSYCH 101

courses.label: PSYCH 339
courses.title: Personnel Psychology
paras: An examination of the following major topics in personnel psychology: employment planning, selection and
recruitment, selection techniques, career development, performance appraisal, training programs, labour relations, compensations systems. Prereq: PSYCH 333

courses.label: PSYCH 340
courses.title: Community Psychology
paras: Theory and practice are integrated in an attempt to identify and to understand the social factors which inhibit or facilitate healthy develapment of the individual. The adequacy of existing social structures and institutions in the treatment of various personal problems is assessed. ‘ Prereq: PSYCH 253
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 341
courses.title: Psychology of Early Childhood Education
paras: An introduction to theories and issues in early childhood education. Topics include issues differentiating preschool programs and application of psychological theory/research to early education. Prereq: PSYCH 211

courses.label: PSYCH 344
courses.title: Theories of Group Counselling
paras: Contemporary theories on the therapeutic application of group processes. Issues Such as group development, leader skills and training, selection of members, problems encountered in both process and outcome research will be examined.
Prereq: PSYCH 101
Offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 353
courses.title: Aggression and Social Conttict
paras: This course will examine the genetic, physiological, and social causes of aggression, with the emphasis on social-psychological causes.
Prereq: PSYCH 253

courses.label: PSYCH 354
courses.title: Interpersonal! Processes in Critical Situations
paras: The course will examine reactions to victims of misfortunes such as serious physical and mental illness, natural disaster, poverty and discrimination. Prereq: PSYCH 253 °

courses.label: PSYCH 355
courses.title: Personality Theory
paras: An examination and evaluation of some of the outstanding theories of personality.
Prereq: PSYCH 101, Cross-listed as PSYCH 322A.

courses.label: PSYCH 356
courses.title: Contemporary Approaches to the Study of Personality
paras: An examination and evaluation of current research in Personality focusing on such topics-as intrinsic motivation, self concept, emotion, locus of control, etc. Prereq: PSYCH 355

courses.label: PSYCH 357
courses.title: Psychopathology
paras: The nature and origin of deviant behaviour.
Prereq: PSYCH 101, Cross-listed as

courses.title: Special Subjects

Prereq: Consent of instructor.

courses.label: PSYCH 370
courses.title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
paras: An examination of the influence of cultural differences on perceptualcognitive processes, personality characteristics, and psychopathology. Prereq: A minimum of two half courses in Psychology.

courses.label: PSYCH 372
courses.title: Environmental Psychology
paras: This course is intended to increase the awareness and understanding of the impact of the environment on human: behaviour and experience. Topics to be discussed include: spacing, territoriality, crowding, subjective impressions of environments, and research paradigms. Prereg: PSYCH 101 and 207 or permission of instructor.
Offered at St. Jerome's College. ..

Prereq: PSYCH 201 and one of PSYCH 355 or 357

courses.label: PSYCH 410
courses.title: History and Systems
paras: An examination of current theoretical approaches to psychological problems present in an historical context.

courses.label: PSYCH 422
courses.title: Principles and Practice in Early Childhood Education Il
paras: An examination of the various aspects of planning and administration in early childhood education programs. Topics include: Practical applications of Piaget’s theory; parent education. Prereq: PSYCH 322 and 323.

courses.label: PSYCH 423
courses.title: Practicum in Earty Childhood Education II
paras: Practicum for advanced students in early childhood education. The course requires 6 hours of field work per week in preschool, kindergarten or daycare settings. Must be taken concurrently with Psychology 422.
Prereq: PSYCH 322 and 323.

courses.label: PSYCH 425
courses.title: Practicum in Early Childhood Education
paras: B For advanced students in early childhood education. The course requires 6 hours of field work per week in preschool, daycare, or kindergarten settings over two terms. In addition, students are required to participate in 6 complete weeks (full days) in block placements during the academic year. Must be taken concurrently with PSYCH 422. Pass/Fail Grading Prereg: PSYCH 322 and 325

courses.label: PSYCH 440
courses.title: Group and Individuat Counselling
paras: The practice of counselling in terms of current psychological theories and research. The demonstration and development of these concepts are aided by persona! participation, exercises, role play and videotape stimulation.
Prereq: PSYCH 355, 357, 344 and 334 or suitable alternative and permission of instructor.

Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: PSYCH 498
courses.title: Senior Honours Essay - Review Paper
paras: Each student will work under the direction of a member of the department on a critical integrative review of an issue in research of literature. The result of this review will be presented in the form of a thesis, which will be critically examined by members of the department.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: PSYCH 120R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: Basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science, with special emphasis on social aspects of behaviour. Topics may include the nervous system, perception, learning, memory, cognition, motivation, emotion, development, personality, social influences, psychopathology and psychotherapy.

courses.label: PSYCH 121R
courses.title: Introductory Psychology (Special , Topics)
paras: A more in-depth study of selected
topics introduced in PSYCH 120R.
Prereq: PSYCH 120A.

courses.label: PSYCH 220R
courses.title: Soclal Psychology
paras: Examination of psychological principles involved in individual - society interaction. Topics may include research methods, self, sexual attitudes and behaviour, person perception, attitudes, affiliation, aggression, altruism, groups, environment and behaviour, toneliness, social psychology and legal process. (Cross-listed with PSYCH 253.)
Prereq: An introductory psychology course.

courses.label: PSYCH 221R
courses.title: Interpersonal Interaction
paras: A consideration of selected theories of interpersonal interaction. Topics include E. Goffman, non-verbal communication, H.S. Sullivan, transactional anatysis, the double-bind theory, R.D. Laing, the basic dimensions of interpersonal behaviour, and social exchange. (Crass-listed with PSYCH 254.)
Prereq: PSYCH 220R or PSYCH 253.

courses.label: PSYCH 322R
courses.title: Personality Theory
paras: An examination of the major theories of personality including consideration of the psychoanalytic, dispositional, humanistic, and behaviouristic models. (Cross-listed with PSYCH 355.)
Prereq: An introductory psychology course.

courses.label: PSYCH 323R
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology (Psychopathology)
paras: A survey of concepts, theory, and research dealing with the nature and etiology of behavioural abnormality. Topics include neurosis, schizophrenia, depression, psychophysiological and behavioural disorders.
(Cross-listed with PSYCH 3857.) Prereq: An introductory psychology course.

courses.label: PSYCH 334
courses.title: Theories of individual Counselling Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods, theories, and problems in Individual Counselling Psychology.
Prereq: An introductory psychology course.

courses.label: PSYCH 367R
courses.title: Special Topics In Psychology
paras: One or more half courses will be offered fram time to time as announced by the Social Development Studies Program. Subjects will be dependent upon special research and/or instructional interests of faculty.

courses.label: PSYCH 369R
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Counselling Psychology
paras: An in-depth study of special topics arising in PSYCH 334(R).
Prereq: PSYCH 334(R).
Social Development Studies majors only.

courses.label: PSYCH 398R
courses.title: Independent Study
paras: An independent in-depth study of a selected area of concern to the student within the discipline of psychology. Available to individuals or small groups of third or fourth year Social Development Studies majors and arranged with one of the faculty members from the program.
Prereq: Permission of Undergraduate Officer.

courses.label: REC 100
courses.title: Introduction to the Study of Leisure and Recreation
paras: An overview of the total field of recreation emphasizing the understanding of leisure phenomena and implications for contemporary society.

courses.label: REC 101
courses.title: Introduction to Leisure Services
paras: An introduction to various leisure service agencies and the services provided. Field trips to municipalities, specialized institutions, and voluntary agencies.

courses.label: REC 200
courses.title: Theories of Play
paras: A critical analysis of definitions, concepts and assumptions of classical, recent and modern theories of play with - implications for research strategies, programming and planning for play.

courses.label: REC 201
courses.title: Leisure and the Social Sciences
paras: Examination of modern methodological and theoretical approaches to the study of leisure behaviour with emphasis upon the socio-cultural, sociopsychological and economic dimensions.

courses.label: REC 203
courses.title: An Introduction to the Sociology of
paras: Sport (Kin 252) .
An introduction to the characteristics, processes and problems of sport as a social system. In addition, the social psychological aspects of sport involvement are considered.
Prereq: SOC 101

courses.label: REC 204
courses.title: Leisure and Recreation in Historicat Perspective
paras: Analysis of socio-cultural determinants which have influenced Canadian Leisure behaviour.
Prereq: REC 100 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 210
courses.title: Organization and Administration of Recreation Services
paras: The organization and administration of recreation on federal, provincial and municipal levels; legislation, financing, budgeting, problem solving, public relations, administrative practices and departmental organization with particular emphasis on the municipal level.

courses.label: REC 220
courses.title: Recreation Program Development
paras: A study of the scope of community recreation programs and the factors involved in program leadership. Emphasis will be placed on the goals in recreation for the leader and participant, effective leadership of individuals and groups, individual and group creativity.

courses.label: REC 230
courses.title: Introduction to Outdoor Recreation
paras: A study of outdoor recreation in relation to contemporary lifestyles, natural and human resource systems. Includes the examination of outdoor settings as an integral part of an outdoor recreation continuum. inctudes the role of selected governmental and non-governmental bodies.

courses.label: REC 241
courses.title: Administration of Camping and Outdoor Education
paras: The philosophy and objectives of camping and outdoor education; administration, organizing, planning, staff, relationships, leadership training, trends in camping and outdoor education. The emphasis in this course will be the place of the resident camp in education and recreation.
Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 250
courses.title: Introduction to Recreation for Special Populations
paras: Examines the philosophical, theoretical and empirical frameworks of recreation as a therapeutic service and process to individuals with physical, emotional and intelectual disabilities.
Course Descriptions 395
Recreation

courses.label: REC 252
courses.title: Recreation and Mental Retardation
paras: An analysis of the motoric and psychosocial behavioral dimensions specific to the retarded with direct and obvious applicability to the planning, implementing and evaluating of recreational programs.
Prereq: REC 250, PSYCH 312

courses.label: REC 253
courses.title: Recreation and Physical Disabilities
paras: The psycho-social aspects of physical disabilities will be analysed, with special tocus given to the planning, implementing and evaluating of leisure activities. Prereq: REC 250, permission of instructor

courses.label: REC 254
courses.title: Recreation and Mental Health
paras: A psycho-social analysis of the determinants and consequences of recreative behaviour as related to positive and negative mental heaith, discussing in detail. structure. semiotic factors and interaction patterns Prereq: REC 250

courses.label: REC 270
courses.title: Statistical Techniques Applied to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction to descriptive and inferential statistics and the interpretation of data. A major consideration of the course is the use of statistics in the solution of problems in recreation and leisure.

courses.label: REC 300
courses.title: Philosophy of Leisure
paras: Examination of major philosophical themes through the ages with reference to contemporary viability and effect upon social behaviour.
Prereq: Consent of instructor, third year standing.

courses.label: REC 301
courses.title: Sociology of Leisure (Soc 347)
paras: Nature and extent of leisure phenomena in contemporary society. Examination of institutional and formal organizational aspects, social role, social research strategies employed in the study of leisure.
Prereq: Two item courses in Sociology

courses.label: REC 302
courses.title: Travel and Tourism
paras: The scope and nature of travel and tourism as contemporary leisure
experiences. Economic, political and social ramifications, research strategies employed. implications for the future. Prereq: REC 301

courses.label: REC 305
courses.title: Social Psychology of Leisure
paras: A study of the social psychological determinants and implications of the human use of discretionary time. The leisurely use of this time as well as specific play-forms and diversionary pursuits such as art, wilderness and high risk activities. humour, day dreaming, hobbies and gambling will be examined.
Prereq: PSYCH 101 and REC 201

courses.label: REC 311
courses.title: School Recreation
paras: An analysis of the relationship between recreation and education with particular emphasis on the sponsoring of community recreation programs by education authorities including leisure education and co-curriculum activities Prereq: REC 210

courses.label: REC 312
courses.title: Recreation and Community Action
paras: The role of the citizen in recreation systems with regard to social change. Students will examine models for social change which interect with recreation systems and power relationships between citizen's groups and recreation systems.
Prereq: REC 210

courses.label: REC 316
courses.title: Principles of Recreation Planning
paras: An exploration of alternative approaches to the planning of recreation opportunities. The demand for and supply of recreation opportunities; standards, models and systems; recreation planning policies and agencies; and selected recreation planning issues. Prereq: PLAN 156 or a full credit in Geography, or consent of instructor.

courses.label: REC 320
courses.title: Evaluation of Recreational Programs
paras: Evaluation procedures and techniques applicable to recreation programs are examined in detail. Specification of objectives, development of practical recording procedures and experimental analysis are stressed. Students conduct fieid evaluations in local community agencies.
Prereq: REC 270

courses.label: REC 321
courses.title: Selected Topics in Recreation
paras: The study of particular topics pertaining to recreation. Course topics will be announced in advance, but will not be offered on a regular basis.
Prereq: Consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 331
courses.title: Outdoor Education in Recreation
paras: The present status of outdoor education in modern society; government functions and policies related to outdoor education services; the planning and administration of outdoor education activities. Current problems. Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 332
courses.title: Theory and Practice in Outdoor Recreation
paras: Emphasis on methods and techniques for the selection, development, and implementation of programs and projects through the utilization of diverse and unique natural settings and environments.
Prereq: REC 230

courses.label: REC 334
courses.title: Park Management
paras: Basic administrative procedures in park management. Operational techniques are examined together with general policies of acquisition, operation and development.
Prereq: REC 210, REC 230 or equivalent

courses.label: REC 361
courses.title: Aging and Leisure
paras: Social parameters of the aging process with particular reference to the Leisure Service Industry.
Prereq: REC 301

courses.label: REC 370
courses.title: Directed Study in Special Topics
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a

courses.label: REC 371
courses.title: Research Designs Applicable to Leisure Studies
paras: An introduction to the methods and techniques of research as applied to leisure studies and services. Generai consideration will be given to the technical problems involved in various stages of research methodology with emphasis on the logic underlying the research process.
Prereq: REC 270

courses.label: REC 372
courses.title: Introduction to Statistical Problem Solving by Computer
paras: This is an applications oriented course which prepares the nonmathematical student to use the computer as a research tool. Topics include aids for Statistical analysis and the preparation of documents such as reports and theses. The course provides sufficient background for application to other problems specific to the individual’s field.
Prereq: A one term Statistics course

courses.label: REC 399
courses.title: Seminar in Recreation and Leisure
paras: An in-depth analysis of the current major issues and trends.
Fourth year Departmental students only.

courses.label: REC 401
courses.title: The Economics of Recreation
paras: A critical examination of the applications of market and non-market segmentation, valuation, and related concepts to recreation and leisure. Course content is based on recent research methods and findings from the field of leisure studies.
Prereq: Third year standing, ECON 101 or permission from instructor

courses.label: REC 402
courses.title: Colloquium on Religion and Leisure
paras: Not offered 1982-83

courses.label: REC 406
courses.title: Comparative Recreational Systems
paras: A study of multi-national recreation systems. Course meets on Campus and in the field in other countries. Fuil term study over a period of 6-8 weeks. Laboratory fee varies with field observation.

courses.label: REC 410
courses.title: Planning of Recreation Facilities
paras: A course to introduce the students to the planning, design and layout of recreation areas and facilities. Prereq: REC 210 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 432
courses.title: Interpretation
paras: Concepts, philosophy and practices of interpretation relative to understanding the use of the natural environment. Prereg: REC 332 or consent of the instructor

courses.label: REC 434
courses.title: Advanced Park Management
paras: A study of policies, procedures, and practices relative to the management of natural resources. Emphasis is placed on an ecological systems approach to management as it relates to parks at all levels of government.
Prereq: REC 334

courses.label: REC 435
courses.title: Recreation Resource Policy
paras: A study of policies, policy development and policy gaps related to recreation resources in Canada. Based on a literature review and discussion of decisionmaking procedures, roles and tools used in the recreation field; students are required to research real and theoretical situations for seminar presentation. Prereq: REC 100 and REC 230 or consent of instructor

courses.label: REC 470
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic supervised by a faculty member. Required of ail students enrolled in the Honours Recreation program. REC 470 includes an approved design and completion of the first segment of the paper. Prereg: REC 270,371 REC 471 requires the completion of the project begun.in 470.

courses.label: SOC 120R
courses.title: Fundamentals of Sociology 1
paras: An examination of the fundamental concepts of sociology and their application in seeking to understand the changing patterns and life-styles taking place specificaily in Canada, and in general, within North American society.

courses.label: SOC 220R
courses.title: The Individual, Society and Religion
paras: An application of sociological analysis to the study of religion. Development of an approach or methodological perspective which can be applied to the study of other social institutions. Prereq: An introductory sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 221R
courses.title: Master Trends in Modern Society
paras: An introduction to the major problems of ubanization and industrialization in modern societies studied within a framework emphasizing social change Illustrations will be drawn from
Course Descriptions 405 Social Development Studies
emergent as well as advanced societies. Prereg: An introductory sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 225R
courses.title: Race and Culture in the Third World 1

courses.label: SOC 226R
courses.title: Race and Culture in the Third World 2

courses.label: SOC 327R
courses.title: Minority Status in Canadian Society
paras: A sociological appraisal of the fundamental concepts and issues
pertaining to minority groups in
Canadian society. The influences of ethnicity, social origins, religion, racial factors and social status will be examined as factors which determine social mobility.
Prereq: An introductory sociology course and second year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 328R
courses.title: Canadian Ethnic and Cultural Minorities
paras: An examination of the adjustment of Native people, French Canadians, Orientals and other minorities within the Canadian mosaic. The course will analyze modernization, constitutional debates and historical events in terms of their impact on minority adjustments. Prereq: An introductory sociology course and second year standing or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 367R
courses.title: The Sociology of Physical Disability
paras: Examination of the social adaptations of the physically disabled. Particular attention is given to the theoretical tradition which considers physical disability as a form of involuntary deviance which stigmatizes the individual.
Prereq: An introductory sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 368R
courses.title: The Sociology of Spolled Identity
paras: Spoiled identity resulting from deviant status inhibits if not prevents acceptance and social mobility. Consequences of spoiled identity, lowered status positions and deviant criminal and “social” adaptations are © examined from a symbolic interactionist perspective.
Prereq: An introductory sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 369R
courses.title: Custodial and Rehabilitative Institutions
paras: “Total institutions” are concerned with resocialization of “inmates”. The philosophies, organization, goals and effectiveness in modifying and controlling behaviour, of maximum security prisons, mental hospitals, isolated work environments and concentration camps constitute the central focus.
Prereq: An introductory sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 398R
courses.title: Independent Study
paras: An independent in-depth study of a selected area of concern to the student within the discipline of sociology. Available to individuals or small groups of third or fourth year Social Development Studies majors and arranged with one of the faculty members from the program.
Prereq: Permission of Undergraduate Officer.

courses.label: SOC 102
courses.title: Social Problems
paras: An examination of cultural forces that create social problems and failures in personal and institutional adjustments. Specific attention is paid to the problems of emotional disturbance, poverty, delinquency and industrial disruptions in Canadian society.

courses.label: SOC 103
courses.title: Canadian Society
paras: An introductory survey of Canadian society. This course will examine issues in the socio-historical development of Canadian society, its present social structure, organizations and ideologies.

courses.label: SOC 104
courses.title: Social Psychology and Everyday Life
paras: Introducing students to symbolic interaction, a sociological social psychology, this course examines: the impact of culture on socialization experiences; the-development of selfidentities and sociai reputations; and interaction patterns in a variety of casual, occupational and deviance contexts.

Perennial Themes in Social Thought Both classical and recent social theorists are shown to exhibit common preoccupations, e.g. the relation of the individual to society, the foundations of government, survival through productivity and adaptation, society's location in nature and the cosmos.

courses.label: SOC 106
courses.title: Collective Behaviour
paras: The sociological analysis of the behaviour of crowds, mobs, publics and related phenomena and their relationships to social organization and social change.

courses.label: SOC 107
courses.title: Soelal Structure and Character
paras: This course will examine the connections between organized social life and types of personalities found in it. Examples will be drawn from contemporary as well as historical situations.

courses.label: SOC 200
courses.title: Marriage and the Family
paras: A survey of sociological perspectives on’
marriage and the family in urbanindustrial societies. Special attention is given to marriage and the family in Canada. Comparisons with U.S. and Britain will be undertaken.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome’s College.

courses.label: SOC 204
courses.title: Sociology of Adolescence
paras: The social definitions of adolescence in cross-cultural and historical perspective. Social roles of adolescence in the institutional structures of urbanindustrial societies with special emphasis on the family, education, and the economy. The relationship of adolescents’ social roles to processes of social change and stability.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 206
courses.title: Sex Roles
paras: An examination of male and female roles in contemporary Canadian

. society. Current and past roles of both sexes in different societies afe considered. Selected topics of interest include sex role identity and its development, male role change, media images of men and women and men’s and women's liberation.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 209
courses.title: Family Origin and Personal Identity
paras: This course focuses on the intersection of biography and social structure within the family. Application of sociological theory and methods to students’ own family backgrounds will be used to illustrate the social bases of identity. Prereq: SOC 107 or consent of instructor.
Offered at St. Jerome's College.
Course Descriptions
Sociology

courses.label: SOC 214
courses.title: Social Inequality
paras: Analysis of social classes in society including their basis for development, composition and consequences for society, Special attention is given to social stratification in Canada. Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 222
courses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
paras: A systematic analysis and criticism is presented of biological, psychological, psychoanalytical and sociological theories of juvenile delinquency. Attention is given to statistics and
“contemporary research with special
emphasis on the distribution and types of delinquent subcultures.
Prereq: SOC 101 orconsentof + instructor.

courses.label: SOC 223
courses.title: Deviance: Perspectives and Processes
paras: The deviance-making process is examined in a variety of social contexts. Examines the emergence of rules and control agencies, the processes by which persons become involved in deviant activities, and the contingencies affecting persons’ careers as deviants. Prereg: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 224
courses.title: Law and Order: Regulating Deviance
paras: Focusing on the “processes and problematics of social contrat”, this course examines: the conditions affecting the emergence of legal norms; the enforcement of criminal law; and the processing of offenders.
Prereq: SOC 107 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 227
courses.title: Crime and Society
paras: An analysis and criticism of the major theories of criminal behaviour. Emphasis is given to the relationship between social structure and criminal behaviour; types of criminal behaviour such as drug addiction statistics and contemporary research. Special attention is given to Canadian data. Prereg: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 228
courses.title: Sociology of Corr
paras: Decisions to process offenders and the role of socia! factors in the Canadian criminal justice system are critically
4h
examined. Focal issues include police discretion, the legal profession and prison systems.
Prereq: SOC 101

courses.label: SOC 233
courses.title: Social Psychology of Beliefs and Attitudes
paras: Examines the nature of social beliefs and attitudes toward various groups in society, such as ethnic, political and religious groups. Considers the sources, organization and distribution of beliefs and attitudes, and their implications for Canadian society.
Prereq: SOC 101 or PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 235
courses.title: Communication
paras: An analysis of the role of language and other symbol systems in social interaction; the interplay between communication and the social system, the formation of attitudes through language; social and individual disorders as caused by, and reflected in, the breakdown in the communication process. Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 236
courses.title: Social Movements
paras: The sociological analysis of varieties of social movements and their relationships to social organization and social change.
Prereq: SOC 101 ar consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 238
courses.title: Sociology of Marketing Sales
paras: This course considers the (social) processes by which people “do business”. Focusing on day to day
-exchanges, ongoing relationships
within the business and consumer community are examined from an
interactionist perspective.
Prereq: SOC 104 or consent of the Instructor.

courses.label: SOC 242
courses.title: Industrial Sociology
paras: Special emphasis is given in lectures, readings and assignments to the particular problems facing industrial Canada, especially in reference to regionalism, elitism, the multinational enterprise and the probiem of foreign ownership.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 243
courses.title: Occupational Sociology
paras: An introduction to the study of work and occupations; the probiems of occupational choice, occupational socialization and identification; the concepts of career and career mobility: the professionalization process, the nature of professions; the impact of occupation on life styles, leisure and retirement.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 244
courses.title: Adoptive Kinship
paras: The study of adoptive kinship sheds light on the weakening of the western family as in an institution. It also reveals strains that appear to be inherent in the invention and enactment of any new institution.

courses.label: SOC 247
courses.title: Soclology of Death and Dying
paras: The course deals with the current literature on death and dying; also, with the sociological implications of institutional housing of the terminal patient. Patterns of mortality as affecting different social groups and as reflecting differential life chances of individuals in society are described. North American issues of death and dying are considered against an historical background.
Prereq: SOC 101 ar consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 248
courses.title: Health, Iliness, and Society
paras: This course focuses on the social aspects of heaith and illness, including social causes of illness, the social process of becoming ill, and the social consequences of being defined as ill. Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Migration and Society

An international overview of migration, particularly during this century; a survey of statistical sources and theoretical explanations of migration. A section of the course will be on the history of immigration to Canada, migration within Canada, and Canadian immigration policies in the context of the world migration situation.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Course Descriptions 409
Sociology

courses.label: SOC 253
courses.title: Population in Canadian Society
paras: Study of the basic demographic processes in the population of Canada. Demographic implications for selected social institutions. Use of Canadian enumeration and registration data. Emphasis on immigration and immigration policy.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 254
courses.title: Comparative Social Structure
paras: General theoretical and methodological issues facing comparative sociology: comparative methods at work in the treatment of Western and non-Western societies (including Canada).
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Third World Development
An analysis of issues of social and economic development in selected areas of the Third World, including Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 256
courses.title: Ethnic and Racial Relations
paras: Relations between different racial and cultural groups, analysis of majorityminority group status with special reference to Canada.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: SOC 264
courses.title: Sociology of Religion
paras: Religion is defined broadly and its relation to phenomena like totalitarian movements, psychoanalysis and drug experience examined. The features common to all religions are explained, viz. myth, dogma, church, ritual, ethics, and religious experience.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: SOC 265
courses.title: Political Sociology
paras: The sociologicat analysis of the institutionalization of power, political movements, parties, conflict and its accommodation.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 267
courses.title: Soclology of the Contemporary University
paras: How have recent demographic and economic changes in North America affected the organization and goals of higher learning? This course explores organizational crises and various attempts at containing and managing them.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 271
courses.title: Introductory Sociological Theory
paras: An examination of the object and function of sociological theory in social research. Types of sociological theories. Discussion of selected classics of sociological theory.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 280
courses.title: Social Statistics and Social Indicators
paras: A first course in sociological statistics, sampling, central tendency, probability, covariance, as illustrated in specifically sociological data.
Prereq: SOC 1017 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 281
courses.title: Methods |
paras: An introductory survey of the research techniques employed by sociologists. The formulation of research designs appropriate to various kinds of intellectual problems in social science is stressed.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 282
courses.title: Methods I!
paras: Continuation of Methods |. The course involves a field project, together with classroom work emphasizing the critical evaluation of research reports.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 302
courses.title: Comparative Sociology of Youth
paras: The aim of this course is mainly to study the prevailing patterns and resulting problems connected with the ways in which different societies react to the emergence of new generations. Concentrates on an analysis of the 1960s.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

courses.label: SOC 329
courses.title: Crime as Business
paras: Examines the inter-relatedness of crime and business, looking not only at the extent to which (1) crime represents business for its practitioners and (2) the criminal activities of legitimate business people, but also (3) the agencies regulating crime.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one Sociology course in the 220 series.

courses.label: SOC 340
courses.title: Complex Organizations
paras: Examines the role of large-scale organizations in industrial society, and their impact and influence. Illustrations will be drawn from commerce and industry, as well as education, health services and government.
Prereq: SOC 101 and SOC 242.

courses.label: SOC 342
courses.title: Sociology of Industrial Relations
paras: Using sociological concepts and theories, the course will examine the nature of the relationship between employers and employees, current issues facing unions and management, and the character of accommodation which may be realized between the two. Prereqg: SOC 101 and SOC 242.

courses.label: SOC 343
courses.title: Sociology of Health Care
paras: Examination of the organizations which provide health care, including assumptions under which they operate, interactive roles played by all members, including patients, alternative arrangements for providing health care, and the social positions held by health professionals.
Prereq: SOC 101 and SOC 248
SOC 344.
Aging, the Aged and Leisure: A Sociologicat and Social Psychological Perspective

Employing a sociological and psychological frame of reference, the process and problems of aging are analyzed. Special emphasis will be given to the problems of leisure time in the later years of life. (Same as KIN 352 and REC 361). : Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course.
Course Descriptions
Sociology

courses.label: SOC 347
courses.title: Sociology of Leisure
paras: Nature and extent of leisure phenomena
. in contemporary society. Examination
of institutional and formal organization aspects, social role, social research strategies employed in the study of leisure. (Same as REC 301).
Prereq: Two term courses in sociology.

courses.label: SOC 348
courses.title: Sport in Society
paras: An introduction to the sociology of sport. Utilizing the major frames of reference of the social sciences, the function of sport in contemporary society is examined. (Same as REC 303 and KIN 452).
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 348
courses.title: Sport in Society
paras: An introduction to the sociology of sport. Utilizing the major frames of reference of the social sciences, the function of sport in contemporary society is examined. (Same as REC 303 and KIN 252).
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 354
courses.title: World Population Problems Comparative Analysis of population
paras: problems across societies. Focus is on social institutions and their relationships to population. Emphasis on fertility and family planning. Prereq: SOC 101 and SOC 253.

courses.label: SOC 364
courses.title: Social Change
paras: A systematic review and analysis of sources, patterns, processes, and consequences of social change in developing countries, the role of ideas, and the breakdown and reorganization of social structure.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one ather Sociology course.
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: SOC 366
courses.title: Urban Soclotogy
paras: The comparative study of urbanization as a process; the culture and organization of cities, urban problems; special attention is given to industrial cities of Canada, with comparative reference to the principal cities of Western societies.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 371
courses.title: Philosophy of Social Science
paras: Problems about the fundamental methods and aims of the social sciences generaily, the problems specific to Psychology, Sociology, Political Science, etc., and their relations to one another will be considered. (Same as PHIL 362.)
Prereq: Some previous work in a Social Science or in Philosaphy.

courses.label: SOC 380
courses.title: Qualitative Methods: Field Techniques
paras: An application of symbolic interactionist theory, this course examines the contingencies affecting data collection and analysis of on-going group life. While doing field work, students have an opportunity to examine basic features of interactionist thought.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course.

courses.label: SOC 381
courses.title: Quantitative Methods
paras: Design and data analysis in contemporary sociological research, with an emphasis on the analysis of secondary data and computer applications.
Prereq: SOC 101 and SOC 280.
The Development of Sociological Theory
Development of sociological theory in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Emphasis is on the European tradition, although selective attention is given to North American theorists.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course (SOC 271 is recommended).

courses.label: SOC 406
courses.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
paras: Development of sociological theory in the 20th century. Included is discussion of current theoretical work.
Prereq: SOC 101 and one other Sociology course (SOC 271 is recommended).

paras: Required of all Honours students in Sociology or by election by Joint Honours students in their fourth year. For students electing Honours Sociology (Canadian Studies), the essay should bear on some topic of particular sociolagical significance for Canadian society.
Prereq: Fourth year Sociology Honours.

courses.label: SOC 190G
courses.title: Sociology of Dissent
paras: A study of social change and innovation from the perspective of the role of individuals who dissent from the dominant norms and institutions. Jesus, Conrad Grebel, Marx, Woodsworth and King will be considered among others.

courses.label: SOC 207G
courses.title: Sociology of Education
paras: This course is designed for Co-op and Regular students who plan to enter the teaching field. Attention will be focused on the concepts and theories of sociology as they apply especially to the educational system.
Prereq: SOC 101 or consent of instructor.

SOC 208) FW 3C 05
Education and Native Peoples

An examination of some of the limitations and alternatives to formal schooling employed mainly by Canadian and Australian indigenous groups (Indian, Inuit, and other aboriginal groups). Special emphasis is placed on skill training and the group’s search for identity.
Catholic Sociological Thought

An analysis of the distinctive emphasis and perspectives which characterize contemporary sociolagical theory in Catholic cultures. The course will focus on theories of the family, the community, human sexuality, politics and the economy.

An examination of sociological research and theory in the field of mental illness, especially as it relates to the family. Such topics as psychiatric hospitals, public attitudes and social stigma, aftercare and rehabilitation, and the epidemiology of mental illness will be examined..

The majority of Systems Design courses are given on the basis of three formal lectures and one tutorial hour each week. The department endeavours to ensure that the formal course schedule remains below 30 hours per week in each term.
